### test_algorithm.das

- `test_erase_all` - erase_all removes every occurrence of a value and leaves the array unchanged when the value is absent

- `test_intersection` - intersection of two sets holds exactly the shared keys, empty when nothing is shared or either side is empty
- `test_union` - union of two sets holds every key of both, and an empty side adds nothing
- `test_difference` - difference holds the keys of the first set missing from the second, all of them when disjoint and none for a subset
- `test_identical` - identical is true only for sets with the same keys, regardless of insertion order

- `test_topological_sort` - topological_sort puts each node after the nodes it must follow in a diamond graph and keeps every node

### uncategorized_gc.das

Regression: Boris's original failure case.  Initializing a value-annotation handle (``ManagedValueAnnotation<T>``) field with ``= default<T>`` triggers an ``ExprMakeLocal`` defaulting path. In the AOT emitter, the resulting stack-temp expression carries ``flags.ref = true`` but ``isRefType = false`` (POD), so ``describeCppTypeEx`` emitted ``T *`` via the ``substitute_ref=true`` local-var pre-decl path while the consumer expected ``T &`` -- a pointer-vs-reference mismatch that broke AOT C++ compilation.  This test must compile under AOT and produce the expected runtime result. It deliberately uses ``= default<clock>`` without the ``@safe_when_uninitialized`` workaround Boris applied at the source level, so a regression in the narrow stack-temp codegen surfaces here.

- `test_default_value_handle_field` - A value-annotation handle field initialized with default<T> compiles in AOT and holds its default

### test_lineinfo_ranges.das

Regression for three LineInfo range bugs (see utils/internal/lineinfo-audit): 1. ExprLet.atInit used to include the lexer-synthesized statement-terminating semicolon, overshooting one phantom column past the end of line. 2. Closure/block-arg bodies started one column early — the hidden mid-rule action before '{' in expression_block leaked its zero-width between-token location into the block span via ast_makeBlock. 3. Class-method bodies are wrapped in a synthesized ExprBlock/ExprWith that was stamped with the method-NAME token range instead of the body's span.

- `test_lineinfo_ranges` - let atInit and block spans match the source text
- `test_lineinfo_ranges_gen1_eof` - a v1 block closed by the end of file ends at its last statement
- `test_parse_file_gen1_pre_infer` - v1 make-syntax and its spans survive parsing before inference

### uncategorized_rtti.das

A bare `return` inside a block exits THE BLOCK only. The interpreter's invokeEx code0 fast path handed enumerators (for_each_function et al.) the closure body's single statement WITHOUT the SimNode_ClosureBlock epilogue that clears stopForReturn — so the first firing return killed the remaining iterations AND leaked the stop flag into the calling function, silently skipping its tail (rst.das documents() lost every Uncategorized function this way). The single-statement and multi-statement closures below are semantically identical; they must count the same. JIT and AOT were always correct — this is an interpreter-only regression rail.

- `test_closure_block_return` - a return inside a closure block is handled correctly for a single closure, several closures and a tail statement
- `test_collect_deps_empty_no_crash` - collecting the dependencies of a function with none does not crash
- `adapter_explicitly_includes_default_callbacks` - the C++ adapter lists the default callbacks it explicitly includes
- `adapter_unknown_default_callback_is_an_error` - naming an unknown default callback for the C++ adapter is an error
- `test_describe_purity` - describe reports the purity of a type
- `test_describe_shared_element_types` - describe reports shared element types once

## cuda/

### test_cuda_emit.das

- `test_cuda_signature` - The emitted CUDA carries the pointer struct, entry point, launch bounds and unpacking, passes the args struct by value with methods as __device__ functions, and routes precise f32 operations through the correctly rounded intrinsics.
- `test_cuda_constructs` - The emitted CUDA spells vectors, control flow with loop hints and the math names, with the right operators, swizzles and bitcasts.
- `test_cuda_constructs_device` - The emitted CUDA spells shared memory, barriers, warp-shuffle subgroup ops, the half family, free functions with generic twins, atomics, constant tables and pointer locals.
- `test_cuda_lifts` - Aliased bindings share one slot, struct elements lower to declarations and field access, and the KHR tiles emit fragment structs, lane gathers and mma.sync.
- `test_cuda_wg_tiles` - The workgroup tiles emit shared A and B structs, per-warp accumulator slots, the layout object and the lane walks.
- `test_cuda_intrinsics` - The CUDA-only tier emits cp.async, ldmatrix, the scaled accumulate, the named barrier, byte_perm, clock32 and inline PTX, and the FP4 rung emits e2m1 fragments and the block-scaled mma.
- `test_cuda_packs` - The pack family emits the expected CUDA text.
- `test_cuda_pins` - The entry override, float exchange, unroll count, constant urange, swizzled store and const pointee each emit their pinned CUDA spelling.
- `test_cuda_no_include` - No emitted CUDA text includes a header.
- `test_cuda_compile_gate` - Every fixture emitted CUDA text compiles through NVRTC for this card.

### test_cuda_oracle.das

- `test_arith_gpu_vs_cpu` - uint, int and float arithmetic run on the GPU equal the CPU reference.
- `test_precise_gpu_vs_cpu` - A precise kernel f32 sums, products and quotients on the GPU equal the CPU reference bit for bit.
- `test_axpy_gpu_vs_cpu` - A kernel using the args struct and a method gives the same results on the GPU as the CPU reference.
- `test_vec_gpu_vs_cpu` - Vector arithmetic, swizzles and converts on the GPU equal the CPU reference.
- `test_control_gpu_vs_cpu` - Control flow on the GPU gives the same results as the CPU reference.
- `test_math_gpu_vs_cpu` - The math whitelist on the GPU matches the CPU reference under fastmath.
- `test_half_gpu_vs_cpu` - The half family on the GPU equals the CPU reference.
- `test_reduce_gpu` - Warp reductions, shared memory and the id builtins on the GPU equal hand-computed values.
- `test_diverge_gpu` - A lane-pair shuffle, first broadcast and elect inside a guard that half the warp skips give the hand-computed values on the GPU.
- `test_userfns_gpu` - Free functions over buffers, shared memory and references on the GPU equal hand-computed values.
- `test_alias_gpu_vs_cpu` - Aliased bindings on the GPU, one buffer per binding, equal the CPU reference with one array per view.
- `test_blocks_gpu_vs_cpu` - Struct elements and vector lanes indexed at run time on the GPU equal the CPU reference.
- `test_packs_gpu_vs_cpu` - The pack family on the GPU equals the CPU reference.
- `test_coop_gpu` - The KHR tiles on the GPU equal a CPU reference GEMM for every layout and accumulator.
- `test_cm2_gpu` - The workgroup tiles on the GPU equal a CPU reference through every form.
- `test_cm2w8_gpu` - The eight-warp workgroup tiles with column-owned accumulators give the CPU-reference row reduce through scratch and block-wide convert.
- `test_intrin_fp4_gpu` - The FP4 tensor rung block-scaled e2m1 product through cp.async and ldmatrix equals the CPU sum, and its conversions equal their CPU bodies.
- `test_cm2i8_gpu` - The int8 workgroup tiles s32 products of two k windows, scaled per row and column off shared arrays, equal the CPU reference.
- `test_intrin_gpu` - The CUDA-only tier (cp.async, ldmatrix, block-scaled int8 product, byte_perm, named barrier under clock32, inline PTX) on the GPU equals the CPU reference.
- `test_cm2deck_gpu` - The decode-in-load form over two k windows with the view B tile reloaded per window equals the CPU reference.
- `test_cm2raw_gpu` - The pipelined decode-in-load over two k windows, the second decoded past the first product, equals the CPU reference.
- `test_cm2dec_gpu` - The decode-in-load form on the GPU equals a CPU reference through the block decode.
- `test_atomics_gpu` - Atomics on the GPU equal hand-computed values.
- `test_tables_lattice_ptrs_gpu_vs_cpu` - Constant tables, the lattice and pointer locals on the GPU equal the CPU reference.
- `test_cm2flash_loads_first_gpu` - Prefetched f16 tiles with both loads ahead of both products leave no copy group in flight after the last product, and a 60-wide extent keeps the plain copy.
- `test_cm2flash_gpu` - The flash tile forms (register A tile, prefetched f16 tiles, packed f16 accumulator) on the GPU equal a CPU reference.

- `test_cuda_reject_wg_walks` - A bad workgroup per-element walk, reduce, product or scaled accumulate fails to compile.

### parity_check.das

- `parity_select_all` - selecting all rows gives identical results with _sql, a plain chain over the SQL source, and a plain array
- `parity_where_filter` - a where filter gives identical results in all three modes
- `parity_project_name` - a single-column projection gives identical results in all three modes

- `parity_first_opt_hit` - first_opt with a match returns the same row in all three modes
- `parity_try_sql_first_ok` - _try_sql with first returns Ok on a populated table with the row all modes agree on
- `parity_try_sql_first_opt_some` - _try_sql with first_opt returns Ok wrapping the same some value as the other modes
- `parity_try_sql_first_opt_none` - _try_sql with first_opt on an empty table returns Ok wrapping none like the other modes
- `sanity_try_sql_first_empty_errs` - _try_sql with first on an empty table returns Err
- `parity_where_symmetric` - a where gives the same rows whether the column is on the left or the right of the comparison, in all three modes
- `parity_where_chained_and` - chained where calls combine as AND identically in all three modes
- `parity_where_starts_with` - a starts_with predicate gives identical results in all three modes
- `parity_where_or_with_string` - an or combined with a string predicate gives identical results in all three modes
- `parity_where_ends_with` - an ends_with predicate gives identical results in all three modes
- `parity_where_contains` - a contains predicate gives identical results in all three modes
- `parity_where_to_lower_eq` - a to_lower comparison gives identical results in all three modes

- `parity_where_abs` - an abs predicate gives identical results in all three modes

- `parity_select_renamed` - a named-tuple select that renames fields gives identical rows in all three modes

- `parity_order_by_single_desc` - order_by descending gives the same price sequence in all three modes
- `parity_order_by_tuple_key` - a tuple order key gives identical rows in all three modes

- `parity_where_order_take` - where, order_by and take give identical rows in all three modes

- `parity_take_then_two_wheres` - two wheres after a take filter the taken rows identically in all three modes

- `parity_full_row_distinct` - full-row distinct gives the same row set in all three modes
- `parity_single_col_distinct` - single-column distinct gives the same value set in all three modes
- `parity_where_select_distinct` - where, select and distinct give the same value set in all three modes
- `parity_union` - union gives the same value set in all three modes
- `parity_intersect` - intersect gives the same value set in all three modes
- `parity_except` - except gives the same value set in all three modes
- `parity_count` - count gives the same number in all three modes

- `parity_join_outer_where_first_inner_limit_leak` - an outer where with first after a join does not leak a limit into the inner source, in all three modes
- `parity_join_with_outer_where` - a join followed by an outer where gives identical rows in all three modes
- `parity_right_filter_join` - a join with a filter on the right source gives identical rows in all three modes

- `parity_join_outer_where_then_count` - a join with an outer where and count gives the same number in all three modes

- `parity_three_table_join_with_outer_where` - a three-table join with an outer where gives identical rows in all three modes

## decs/

### failed_component_value_too_big.das

compile-fail fixture: Setting a component value larger than the component size limit must not compile (error 31400).

### failed_query_eid_ro.das

compile-fail fixture: Writing to a component read through a nested query(eid) block must not compile: that component is read-only.

### failed_set_const_container.das

compile-fail fixture: Setting a component from a constant array must not compile: the array moves into the component, and a constant can't be emptied.

### failed_test_arguments.das

compile-fail fixture: query() blocks with an optional argument that has a default or is not a pointer, or a default or reference on a const argument, must not compile.

### failed_test_empty_template.das

compile-fail fixture: A [decs_template] struct with no fields must not compile: the template needs at least one field.

## depfile/

### test_depfile.das

`daslang -MD -MF <path>` writes what the run read, the way a C compiler's -MD does, and a build system stats that list to decide the run can be skipped. These arms drive a child daslang and read the rule it left: nothing here inspects the recorder, only its output.

- `test_md_names_every_source_the_compile_read` - -MD -MF writes a depfile listing the root, every required module and builtin.das
- `test_target_defaults_to_the_path_without_its_d` - without -MT the depfile target is the depfile path minus its .d suffix, and -MT overrides it
- `test_a_vanished_file_is_not_an_input` - a source that disappeared between two runs is dropped from the merged depfile rule
- `test_a_runtime_read_is_not_an_input` - a file the script reads while running is not listed as a depfile input
- `test_the_environment_arms_a_spawned_process` - DAS_DEPFILE alone makes a spawned daslang write a depfile, with no command-line flag
- `test_excluded_directories_stay_out` - a directory named in DAS_DEPFILE_EXCLUDE contributes no inputs to the depfile
- `test_two_runs_merge_into_one_rule` - two runs with the same -MF and -MT merge into a single rule holding both inputs
- `test_a_target_with_a_drive_letter_merges` - a drive-lettered -MT target keeps its name and merges both runs inputs without listing its own tail

## escape_analysis/

### lattice_escape_tests.das

- `test_alias_local_freed` - an allocation that is only aliased by a local is freed each iteration so the heap does not grow
- `test_return_ownership_freed` - an allocation returned to a caller that consumes it locally is freed, with the sum intact
- `test_return_ownership_transitive` - ownership returned through a chain of calls is still freed by the final consumer
- `test_escaping_control_grows` - an allocation pushed into a global is not freed, so the heap grows as the control case
- `test_param_alias_no_double_free` - a function that aliases its parameter never frees the caller object, so repeated calls stay correct
- `test_capture_into_global_lambda_not_freed` - an allocation captured by a lambda stored in a global is not freed, so later allocations do not overwrite it
- `test_capture_into_local_lambda_sound` - an allocation captured by a local lambda stays valid for every call of the lambda
- `test_returned_lambda_capture_not_freed` - an allocation captured by a returned lambda is not freed before the lambda is invoked
- `test_returned_generator_capture_not_freed` - an allocation captured by a returned generator is not freed while the generator yields
- `test_block_field_use_freed` - an allocation only read through a block field is freed after use
- `test_block_escape_grows` - an allocation that escapes through a block into a global is kept, so the heap grows
- `test_alias_chain_escape_sound` - an allocation that reaches a global through a chain of aliases is not freed
- `test_conditional_escape_sound` - an allocation that escapes on one branch is not freed on either, and the stored objects stay intact
- `test_reassigned_no_double_free` - reassigning a variable that held an allocation never frees the object held by a global anchor
- `test_sibling_mixed` - of two sibling allocations the escaping one stays intact while the other is freed
- `test_return_param_alias_no_double_free` - returning a parameter alias never frees the caller object
- `test_unsafe_local_not_freed` - an allocation whose address is taken in unsafe code is not freed
- `test_lambda_captures_alias_sound` - a lambda that captures an alias of an allocation keeps that allocation alive
- `test_block_aliases_escape_grows` - a block that aliases an allocation into a global keeps it, so the heap grows
- `test_lambda_in_block_sound` - a lambda created inside a block keeps its captured allocation alive
- `test_string_builder_element_freed` - a temporary used only to build a string is freed each iteration
- `test_pea_partial_free_reclaims` - partial escape analysis frees the allocation on the path where it does not escape
- `test_pea_partial_escape_path_ok` - on the escaping path of a partial-escape function the allocation survives with its value intact
- `test_pea_within_block_death_freed` - an allocation that dies within a block is freed at the end of the block
- `test_pea_early_return_freed` - an allocation on a non-escaping early-return path is freed
- `test_pea_early_return_escape_survives` - an allocation on the escaping early-return path survives in the global
- `test_pea_nested_freed` - nested non-escaping branches free their allocation
- `test_pea_multi_freed` - several allocations on non-escaping paths are all freed
- `test_pea_for_source_not_freed` - an allocation used as a for-loop source is not freed while the loop runs

### test_allocate_on_stack.das

- `test_stack_plain_new` - a plain new of a small struct is placed on the stack so the heap does not grow
- `test_stack_ascend_new` - a new with ascend of a small struct is placed on the stack so the heap does not grow
- `test_stack_owning_frees_owned_heap` - a stack-allocated struct frees the heap it owns when it dies
- `test_stack_big_struct_stays_on_heap` - a struct too big for the stack stays on the heap
- `test_stack_multiple_live_objects` - several live stack-allocated objects at once all keep correct values
- `test_stack_multi_variable_let` - a multi-variable let of new objects places each on the stack
- `test_stack_control_grows` - an escaping allocation is not moved to the stack, so the heap grows as the control case

### test_escape_free_frees.das

- `test_escape_free_actually_frees` - an allocation that never escapes is freed each iteration so the heap does not grow
- `test_escape_free_multi_var` - several non-escaping allocations are all freed within a small heap budget
- `test_escape_free_pure_call` - an allocation passed only to a pure builtin is freed
- `test_escape_free_pure_script_call` - an allocation passed only to a pure script function is freed
- `test_escape_free_pure_script_transitive` - an allocation passed through nested pure script functions is freed
- `test_escape_free_under_try_recover` - an allocation inside a try block is freed and the loop result is correct
- `test_escape_free_collects_owned_heap` - freeing an owning struct also collects the heap it owns
- `test_escape_free_control_grows` - an escaping allocation is not freed, so the heap grows as the control case

### perf_time.das

Regression coverage for `ref_time_ticks()` and `get_time_usec(int64)`.  The cross-platform normalization landed via PR #2685 (Windows now returns nanoseconds via QPC, matching POSIX clock_gettime — previously Windows returned raw QPC ticks). These tests pin the post-fix contract: - `ref_time_ticks()` returns a monotonic non-decreasing nanosecond timestamp on every platform. - `get_time_usec(t0)` returns elapsed time in microseconds since `t0` and stays consistent with the `ref_time_ticks` delta. - sleep(N ms) round-trip lands close to N ms (with slack for OS scheduler granularity — Windows is the worst at ~16 ms ticks).

- `test_ref_time_ticks_monotonic` - Successive ref_time_ticks reads never go backwards
- `test_ref_time_ticks_sleep_roundtrip` - A 100 ms sleep measures between 80 and 500 ms in nanoseconds
- `test_get_time_usec_agrees_with_ref_delta` - get_time_usec agrees with the nanosecond delta of ref_time_ticks to within 5 ms
- `test_ref_time_ticks_units_are_nanoseconds` - Equal sleeps produce roughly equal raw tick deltas, so the tick rate is uniform

## flatten/

### no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das

Fold-completeness verification over the ACTUAL compiled output. It compiles REAL flatten units and asserts no const-foldable residual (`x*1`/`x+0`/`x*-1`, an all-const call, a const-condition `?:`, a const `!`) survives in the final post-flatten AST — using `flatten_fold_residuals` (daslib/flatten) — the only fold-completeness check (there is no compile-time flag). Running over compiled output, it covers the `[pixel_shader]` backend path uniformly with `[flatten]` (the single-fold + re-infer loop that left the center-tap `uv + float2(0,0)` residual). Three unit kinds: • every example shader (project-resolved) — the `@pixel_shader` entry function; • _fold_fixtures.das (this dir) — the `[flatten]` reveal-cascade corpus (`*_flat`); • test_flatten_const.das — the const-identity corpus. This is the structural FIRED half of that file's verification; the file itself carries only differential VALUE checks (a missed fold computes the same value, so it needs this residual proof).  Lives in tests/flatten/no_aot/ (excluded from test_aot via tests/.das_test): it requires daslib/flatten at runtime, pulling macro_boost generic instantiations that don't AOT-link in the full-tree batch. Runs in interp + JIT; the residual check is tier-independent.

- `test_flatten_fold` - compiled flatten corpora leave no const-foldable residual in the final AST and show the structural marks each rewrite is meant to leave

### no_aot/test_flatten_inline_accumulator.das

Regression for the inlined-accumulator SSA bug (reported as the `dithering` flatten shader). A `var` accumulator declared inside an INLINED helper and reassigned in a (parallel) loop is uniquified to `__flat_loc_N` by inline_call. ssa_rename_pass must SSA-rename it like a user accumulator — else it stays a self-referential `var __flat_loc_N` whose live `= init` a later DSE strips, leaving a null-init self-ref the shader backend rejects (error[50503] undefined __flat_loc_N). Plain flatten ACCEPTS the self-ref var (it is valid daslang), so a value check alone can't gate this — the structural half asserts the inlined accumulator was SSA-renamed (`__ssa___flat_loc_`), which is present iff ssa_rename processed it.

- `test_flatten_inline_accumulator` - an accumulator declared in an inlined helper is SSA-renamed and the flattened twin matches its original

### no_aot/uncategorized.das

Regression for the helper-inline swizzle bug. flatten inlines a helper that reads a by-value VECTOR parameter through a single-component swizzle (`p.x`). copy_prop then substitutes the call argument into the swizzle base. That argument is a VALUE — arithmetic, or the value-copy of a ref — so the swizzle becomes non-ref, while the `p.x`-of-a-ref-local read it replaced still carried an ExprRef2Value. Before the typer folded ref2value-of-a-value (ast_infer_type.cpp), the generated `_flat` twin failed to compile with error[30921] "can only dereference a reference". Reported as the shaders heal_3d / force_field (examples/flatten); these cover the same shapes in plain flatten. The file COMPILING proves the twins build; the equal() checks prove equivalence.

- `test_flatten_inline_swizzle` - a helper reading a vector parameter through a swizzle inlines into a twin that compiles and matches its original
- `test_flatten_mutcollect` - collect_mutable sees every spelling of a store, and writes_through_argument is false off both ends of the argument list
- `test_flatten_pack` - flatten_pack re-rolls a min reduction into vector variables and bails out on a const-threshold select and an accumulator-dependent lane
- `test_flatten_reentry` - re-running flatten_optimize on an already optimized body hoists new work under fresh preshader and cse names without colliding with existing ones

### no_aot/uncategorized__flatten_hadd_pack_pairs.das

The width-2 hadd path, opt-in via `options _flatten_hadd_pack_pairs = true`: with the floor lowered to 2, a bare pair packs into `hadd2` and plan_groups emits width-2 remainders (5 -> [3,2]). This is +1 node on a node-graph backend but a win in cycles on a SIMD CPU backend — hence opt-in, default width>=3 (see test_flatten_hadd.das). Value approx (the hadd reorders the adds); the structural FIRED proof (`hadd(float2(` / `hadd(float3(` emission) lives in test_flatten_fold.das.

- `test_flatten_hadd_pairs` - with the pack-pairs option a bare pair packs into hadd2 and the twin matches its original beyond float rounding

### no_aot/uncategorized_persistent_heap.das

Pins the ownership rule the flatten optimizer's `unsafe { delete <container> }` sites rest on. `ExpressionPtr` is `Expression?` — a HANDLED C++ type, so its instances never live on the das heap and the container finalizer frees only the buffer. That is what makes it safe to delete an `array<ExpressionPtr>` still holding borrowed tree nodes (the const-fold early return of `make_float_ctor` leaves its lanes un-consumed) and to keep a borrowed node in a plain struct field without `@do_not_delete`. If a release ever puts AST nodes on the das heap, those deletes become live-tree frees and this test is the tripwire — it fails here, not in a shader.  The das-heap arm is the anti-vacuity control: the same measurement over `array<S?>` must show the pointees actually reclaimed, or the AST arm proves nothing.  Lives in tests/flatten/no_aot/: `options persistent_heap` (exact free accounting) is a whole-program policy the AOT batch does not carry.

- `test_flatten_ast_ownership` - deleting a container of AST pointers frees only its buffer while deleting das-heap pointers reclaims the pointees

### test_flatten_const.das

Verification net for the flatten const-optimization arc — two layers per case (numbered per the arc's 5-layer verification framework; Layer 1, the randomized fold-oracle, is deferred to a later arc, hence the 0/2 gap): • VALUE (Layer 0): each `[flatten]` twin must compute identical results to its un-flattened original over a FINITE input grid. On this grid the lossy float folds (`x*0`, `x+0`, `x-0`) preserve `==` equality (`finite*0 == 0`, `x+0 == x`; the bitwise `-0.0`/NaN/inf differences either don't arise here or compare `==`-equal), so plain `equal` suffices — `equal_approx` is reserved for the reassociation arc, where rounding genuinely differs. • FIRED (Layer 2): differential alone can't see a fold that failed to fire — an un-optimized twin computes the same value, so VALUE checks must be paired with a structural proof that the collapse happened. That proof lives in `tests/flatten/no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das`, which compiles THIS file as a unit and asserts `flatten_fold_residuals` is empty on every `*_flat` twin (rejecting any unfolded algebraic identity, all-const call, or const-condition select left behind). (Node-count proof at the backend level lives in the cap_fold_* shaders.) The genuinely-non-folding shapes here — a param-seeded runtime accumulator, or a scalar-broadcast `s * vec(1)` the same_base_type gate must NOT collapse to scalar — are part of that same corpus: their empty residual set proves the check does NOT false-positive on a shape that legitimately does not fold.

- `test_flatten_const` - flatten folds multiply, add and subtract identities and zero products for scalars, vectors and ints, and each twin matches its original over a finite grid

### test_flatten_ctor.das

Twin corpus for the ctor lane algebra. Fold phase: zero-lane kill (`floatN(e…) * constVec` zeroes the ctor lanes under a zero const lane — fast-math for floats, exact for ints) and splat collapse (`v ⊙ floatN(s) → v ⊙ s` for * and / — bit-exact). Fuse phase: lane re-vectorization (`floatN(v.x + c1, v.y + c2, …) → v + floatN(c…)` — bit-exact, the per-lane ops are the same IEEE ops), shared-factor extraction (`floatN(s*a, s*b, s*c) → floatN(a,b,c) * s` — bit-exact), and majority-const compensation (`float3(x*C1, y*C1, z*C2) → float3(x, y, z*(C2/C1)) * C1` — the odd-lane reciprocal rounds → fapprox + fast-math gate). All exact twins compare `equal`; only the compensation twin needs `fapprox`. Structural halves live in tests/flatten/no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das (option-aware oracles) and capability/cap_ctor.shader.

- `test_flatten_ctor` - the ctor lane algebra (zero-lane kill, splat collapse, lane re-vectorization, shared-factor extraction, majority-const compensation) gives twins that match their originals

### test_flatten_differential.das

Differential tests for daslib/flatten: each `[flatten]`-annotated function is run against its generated `<name>_flat` twin over an input grid; the flattened (branchless, call-free) twin must compute identical results.  NOTE: the interpreter's `?:` short-circuits, so these tests prove logical EQUIVALENCE — they do not exercise the branchless "both arms execute" behavior of a real GPU backend. See tests/flatten/README.md.

- `test_flatten_equivalence` - each [flatten] twin of a tail return, early-return guard, nested if with mutation, inlined call chain, whitelisted builtin and unrolled helper computes the same results as its original over an input grid
- `test_flatten_coverage` - twins for rarely exercised lowering branches (unary and ternary wrapping calls, bare blocks, with-scopes, discarded calls and more) compute the same results as their originals and are proven branchless and call-free
- `test_flatten_lift` - a user helper call hidden inside a field, swizzle, struct, tuple or argument expression is inlined, so the twin matches its original and is call-free
- `test_flatten_nested` - twins of nested if and if/else shapes, with early returns and shared accumulators, compute the same results as their originals over a two-dimensional grid
- `test_flatten_loops` - fixed-count loops (constant range or array literal), nested loops and compound assignments unroll into twins that match their originals
- `test_flatten_break_continue` - break and continue inside unrolled loops, alone, nested, folded to constants or beside returns, produce twins that match their originals
- `test_flatten_empty_loop_fold` - a flatten function whose helper loop body is eliminated to empty compiles without crashing the constant folder and its twin matches the original
- `test_predicated_increment_keeps_the_counter_type` - a predicated increment keeps the counter's own type for uint, int64, uint64, float and double counters
- `test_flatten_api` - flatten_function and flatten_fold called from another module's macro honor the caller's whitelist, collapse constant selects and keep or drop side-effecting calls as the source semantics require

### test_flatten_dot.das

Differential net for the PHASE_FUSED horizontal-add → dot re-pack: a sum of same-vector lane reads — bare `v.x`, const-weighted `v.x * c`, negated, repeated — collapses into `dot(v, mask)` with missing lanes masked by 0. The dot reorders the adds and runs hardware-dotted, so floats compare approx (same contract as the mad corpus). The structural FIRED half (a `dot(` call in the twin) lives in no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das.

- `test_flatten_dot` - sums of lanes of one vector are re-packed into a dot product without changing the result beyond float rounding

### test_flatten_hadd.das

Differential net for the PHASE_FUSED horizontal-reduce re-pack (DEFAULT width>=3 policy): a sum of independent scalars (no shared vector base, so the dot fold above can't reach them) collapses into `hadd(floatN(...))` groups of width 3..4 via plan_groups — or `dot(floatN(s), floatN(weights))` when the lanes carry const weights (`a*2 + b*3 + …`). A width-2 tail stays scalar (a bare pair is +1 node on a node-graph backend); the width-2 path is exercised under the option in no_aot/uncategorized__flatten_hadd_pack_pairs.das. The reduce reorders the adds, so floats compare approx (same contract as the dot/mad corpus). The structural FIRED half lives in no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das.

- `test_flatten_hadd` - sums of independent scalars are re-packed into horizontal adds of width three or four and the twins match their originals beyond float rounding

### test_flatten_mad.das

Differential net for the mad disassemble → re-fuse arc and the DEFAULT lerp handling. The fold expands `mad` calls into raw arithmetic (reassoc/CSE see through the operators); the PHASE_FUSED finishing pass re-packs surviving `a*b ± c` into `mad(a,b,c)` and the lerp shape `mad(b-a, t, a)` back into `lerp(a,b,t)`. `lerp` calls are KEPT WHOLE by default (a native-lerp backend computes `(b-a)*t+a` in one instruction); the const-selector identities (`t=0`/`t=1`/ `a==b`) fire directly on the call. The opt-in expansion path (`options _flatten_expand_lerp`) has its own corpus in uncategorized__flatten_expand_lerp.das. Exactness per twin: int twins and same-builtin-both-sides round trips compare exact; ANY float twin comparing raw interp ops against a `mad`/`lerp` builtin compares approx — the vector builtins are hardware-fused (NEON FMLA / x86 FMADD), and even the scalar C++ impls (`a*b + c`, `(b-a)*t + a`) get FMA-contracted by the host compiler, so the rounding is platform-dependent. The FIRED structural proof (an actual `mad`/`lerp` call, no `a*b + c` residual) lives in `no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das` via the fusion arms of `flatten_opt_residuals`.

- `test_flatten_mad` - multiply-add shapes re-fuse into mad and lerp calls for scalar, int and vector twins that match their originals

### test_flatten_opt.das

Differential net for the flatten OPTIMIZE arc (preshader extraction + CSE + regroup-to-share). Hoist/dedup passes are VALUE-EXACT, so their twins compare with exact `equal` (unlike the reassoc arc). Carve-outs compare approx: a twin where PHASE_FUSED packs a mul-add into hardware-fused `mad` (p_vec, the r_* returns), and the regroup twins themselves (re-pairing `C - x` moves the float association). The FIRED proof (a `_preshader_` let on top, a shared `_cse_` let) lives in `no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das` (empty `flatten_opt_residuals`) and the cap_preshader / cap_cse node-count shaders; here we only assert the optimization preserved the result.

- `test_flatten_opt` - preshader extraction, common-subexpression elimination and regrouping keep each twin's result equal to its original

### test_flatten_rcp.das

Twin corpus for the fast-math division rewrites: `x / C → x * (1/C)` (fold arm) and `x / U → x * _preshader(1/U)` (extraction, U uniform). Exactness tiers: a power-of-two reciprocal is exact (`equal`); any other reciprocal rounds, so those twins compare `fapprox` — the rounding is the fast-math contract, `options _flatten_no_fast_math` turns it off (see uncategorized__flatten_no_fast_math.das). A zero divisor keeps the division (no inf literal is minted); integer division is out of scope entirely. The structural FIRED half (no un-rcp'd const/uniform division residual) lives in tests/flatten/no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das via the option-aware oracles; the backend node proof is capability/cap_rcp.shader (one shared per-draw reciprocal).

- `test_flatten_rcp` - division by a constant or uniform is rewritten to multiplication by a reciprocal, exactly for powers of two and to rounding otherwise, and a zero divisor keeps the division

### test_flatten_select_fusion.das

Differential tests for the same-condition select-accumulation fusion (flatten_opt fuse_select_chains). An unrolled loop with a LOOP-INVARIANT guard (`if (uniform) { acc OP= tap }`) emits a chain of selects all on ONE condition; the fusion hoists that condition out of all N selects (strip every link but the last, retarget the tail's false arm to the base). It is bit-exact (the op tree is preserved, not reassociated), so it fires for ANY op in the chain (+/*/min/max/clamp/mad), for non-zero bases, and is NOT fast-math gated. Each twin runs against its original over a grid spanning the guard-false and guard-true sides. The control (`sf_pervar`, guard depends on the loop counter → distinct masks) must NOT fuse but stays value-correct. The structural FIRED proof (select count collapses) lives in tests/flatten/no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das via twin_bodies.

- `test_flatten_select_fusion` - a chain of selects on one loop-invariant guard fuses without changing values, and a per-iteration guard or a division by zero stays correct

### test_flatten_swizzle.das

Differential net for the swizzle lane fold: `ctor(args…).mask` resolves every output lane to its provenance (scalar arg / lane of an opaque vector / const) and re-emits the cheapest equivalent — the base itself, one swizzle, a scalar, a splat, or a narrower ctor. Pure lane selection is bit-exact, so every compare here is EXACT equal. The structural FIRED half lives in no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das.

- `test_flatten_swizzle` - swizzles of constructors fold to the cheapest equivalent lane selection and every twin equals its original exactly

### uncategorized__flatten_expand_lerp.das

Twin corpus for `options _flatten_expand_lerp` — the opt-in lerp disassembly for backends WITHOUT a native lerp instruction. Under the option the fold expands `lerp(a,b,t)` into `(b-a)*t + a` so reassoc/CSE/preshader see through it, and PHASE_FUSED re-packs the surviving `mad(b-a, t, a)` shape back into one `lerp` call — the expand → re-fuse round trip that is OFF by default. Float differentials compare approx (the das lerp builtin is FMA-contracted, the expanded form is raw interp ops — same contract as test_flatten_mad.das). The structural half (round trip survives, the merge shape proves expansion FIRED, uniform bounds split into a preshader mad) lives in no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das.

- `test_flatten_lerp_expand` - with the expand-lerp option, lerp is expanded and re-fused while twins still match their originals and constant selectors still collapse

### uncategorized__flatten_no_fast_math.das

Twin corpus for `options _flatten_no_fast_math` — the user opt-out of flatten's value-changing rewrites. Under the option every gated rewrite (float `x*0`/`x-x`, float reassoc, lerp const-selectors) is SKIPPED, so each twin executes the same op sequence as its original and every differential below compares EXACT `equal` — including the reassoc shapes that need `fapprox` in the fast-math corpus. The bit-exact passes (flattening, predication, preshader extraction, CSE, mad fusion) must still run; the int twins prove the integer folds (exact) still fire. The structural FIRED/SKIPPED half lives in tests/flatten/no_aot/test_flatten_fold.das, which compiles this file as a unit and asserts the gated shapes SURVIVE in the twins while the option-aware oracle (`flatten_fold_residuals` called with the unit's detected `_flatten_no_fast_math` flag) stays clean.

- `test_flatten_nofastmath` - with the no-fast-math option every value-changing rewrite is skipped, so each twin equals its original bit for bit

### uncategorized_no_aot.das

Boundary tests for daslib/flatten: each `_err_*.das` fixture trips a supported-subset boundary; we compile it and assert the specific loud `flatten:` error fires (rather than silently emitting wrong output).

- `test_flatten_boundaries` - each fixture that crosses a supported-subset boundary fails to compile with its specific flatten error

- `test_default_methods` - a default interface method is used when not overridden, can be overridden, and several defaults mix with overrides
- `test_mixed_scenarios` - one object is reachable through every interface of its hierarchy while a different class implements only part of it

### test_interfaces.das

- `test_basic_dispatch` - calls through an interface proxy dispatch to the implementing methods, including return values and state
- `test_multiple_interfaces` - a class implementing two interfaces serves each through its own independent proxy
- `test_lazy_proxy` - an interface proxy is null until first requested and is reused on later requests
- `test_is_operator` - is is true for implemented interfaces and false for ones the class does not implement, including the empty interface
- `test_as_operator` - as returns a working proxy for each implemented interface
- `test_safe_as_operator` - ?as returns a working proxy for a non-null object and null for a null one, for each interface
- `test_empty_interface` - a class can implement an interface with no methods and is and as work on it

### jit_artifacts.das

no_aot: every test here drives the JIT or a JIT-built artifact

- `test_main` - the JIT DLL cache reuses its DLL for an unchanged script and compiles a new one when the script changes
- `test_executable` - JIT-compiled executables for hello world, builtin global init, an init and a block-initialized global in a cloned context, and a function-pointer global run and print the expected output
- `test_jit_lib_shared` - daslang -lib builds a shared library with a C header that a daslang host loads and calls correctly
- `test_jit_lib_static_and_export_all` - a static -lib-export-all build writes its archive and exports every function to its host
- `test_jit_lib_result_slot_is_aligned` - a structure whose alignment exceeds the argument frame's crosses the library boundary intact
- `test_jit_lib_binds_into_a_daslang_host` - a library's export_c comments reach both the C header and the generated daslang bindings, and a daslang host calls it
- `test_jit_lib_runs_the_standalone_fixture` - the AOT standalone fixture also builds as a JIT library and answers the same values
- `test_jit_lib_is_a_guest_of_a_populated_runtime` - a library reaching its own modules works inside a host runtime that already holds modules
- `test_jit_lib_carries_two_module_sets` - two JIT libraries with different module sets coexist in one host
- `test_wasm_finally_return` - a native run takes every exit through a finally once, and the wasm64 cross compile of that shape emits its object
- `test_wasm_idot_lowering` - the wasm64 cross compile lowers idot4 to the pairwise int8 dot with simd128 and no relaxed-simd, and a host compile emits no wasm intrinsic
- `test_cross_target_folds` - the target triple and architecture name fold to the cross target's values for a --jit-target compile and to the host's otherwise
- `test_break_inside_a_try_arm_leaves_the_loop_under_jit` - a break inside a try arm of a loop whose recover arm can panic leaves the loop under -jit on a cold cache and again on the warm one
- `test_guarded_load_through_an_odd_pointer_is_skipped` - a load through an odd int? that a parity test guards is skipped under -jit: the pointer parameter carries no alignment the fold could use
- `test_solid_array_base_is_hidden_from_codegen` - under solid_context the address of a global array a loop indexes, shared or not, reaches code generation hidden in the one-module and the split build, and a scalar global's does not

## json/

### cant_sscan_array_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a temporary array value must not compile: the destination has to be an addressable variable.

### cant_sscan_conditional_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a conditional (cond ? var : temporary) must not compile: a temporary branch cannot be a destination.

### cant_sscan_const_scalar.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a const scalar must not compile: the destination is written, so it cannot be const.

### cant_sscan_const_struct.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a const struct must not compile: the destination is written, so it cannot be const.

### cant_sscan_fallback_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a `pointer ?? temporary` fallback must not compile: the temporary side cannot be a destination.

### cant_sscan_fixed_array_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a fixed-array literal must not compile: a temporary fixed array cannot be a destination.

### cant_sscan_named_destination.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json with a named-tuple argument holding a const destination must not compile: the destination is written, so it cannot be const.

### cant_sscan_scalar_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a function call's scalar result must not compile: a call result is const, not a destination.

### cant_sscan_struct_result.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a function call's struct result must not compile: a call result is a temporary, not a destination.

### cant_sscan_struct_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a struct constructor expression must not compile: a temporary struct cannot be a destination.

### cant_sscan_table_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a default table value must not compile: a temporary table cannot be a destination.

### cant_sscan_vector_value.das

compile-fail fixture: sscan_json into a vector constructor expression must not compile: a temporary vector is const, not a destination.

- `parity_group_by` - group_by over from_json gives the same per-key counts as over an array
- `parity_group_by_first` - taking the first whole row of each group over from_json matches the array result
- `parity_aggregates` - sum, count, min and max over from_json match the array results
- `parity_distinct` - distinct over from_json gives the same values as over an array
- `parity_first_last_single` - first, last and single over from_json return the same rows as over an array
- `parity_element_at` - element_at and element_at_or_default over from_json match the array results
- `parity_any_all_contains` - any, all and contains over from_json match the array results
- `parity_take_skip` - skip and take over from_json match the array result

- `test_roundtrip_method_not_found_error` - an error envelope built for a parsed request carries its id and the method-not-found code
- `test_roundtrip_batch` - a batch made by make_batch parses back to the same requests

### test_strict_mode.das

- `test_strict_rejects_missing_jsonrpc` - strict parse_request rejects a request without the jsonrpc field with -32600
- `test_strict_rejects_non_2_0` - strict parse_request rejects jsonrpc values other than the string 2.0
- `test_strict_preserves_id_in_response` - a strict-mode rejection keeps the request id in its error envelope
- `test_strict_batch` - strict parse_batch rejects only the entries that break strict rules

## language/

### annotations.das

- `test_struct_annotations` - a struct's annotation and its int, float, bool and string arguments read back through context debug info, with only the escaped quote unescaped in a string argument
- `test_field_annotations` - each struct field's own annotation arguments read back through debug info, and an unannotated field reports none
- `test_function_annotations` - a function's [export] annotation is visible in the context's function debug info
- `test_enum_annotations` - an enum with no annotations has EnumInfo with an annotation count of zero
- `test_resolve_annotation` - resolve_annotation turns a debug-info annotation back into the live structure annotation object
- `test_deprecated_structure_for_each_annotation` - the deprecated structure_for_each_annotation still yields the env-resolved annotation with its reconstructed arguments
- `annotation_int64_typeinfo_retains_full_values` - typeinfo struct_get_annotation_argument returns full 64-bit signed and unsigned annotation literals unchanged
- `annotation_int64_runtime_reflection_retains_full_values` - runtime reflection returns 64-bit struct and field annotation arguments as tInt64 / tUInt64 with their full values
- `annotation_unsigned_literals_are_uint64` - hex and unsigned annotation literals of every width come back as uint64, through typeinfo and through runtime field reflection
- `int64_minimum_literal_in_expressions` - the int64 minimum literal parses in an expression to the bit pattern 0x8000000000000000
- `signed_annotation_values_survive_reflection` - negative int and float annotation arguments, and negative zero, keep their sign through typeinfo and runtime field reflection
- `test_typeinfo_annotations` - typeinfo struct_has_annotation, struct_has_annotation_argument and struct_get_annotation_argument answer for a struct's annotation at compile time
- `test_arch_annotation_compiles` - an [arch] citation on a function, a struct or a class compiles and changes no behavior, alone, twice, or beside another annotation
- `test_unused_arguments_annotation` - [unused_argument(b, c)] lets a function leave those arguments unread without a warning, and it still computes from the rest
- `test_each_annotation_instance_patches_once` - two instances of one patching function annotation on a function each apply their patch once
- `test_far_overrides_abstract` - an abstract method's field carries the abstract and inherited bits through clone and override, and the overriding body dispatches

### arrays.das

- `test_array` - an int array keeps its elements through fill, move-out and move-back, two-array parallel for, push, resize, reserve and erase, and push, push_from, push_clone_from and emplace_from append struct arrays and fixed arrays
- `test_dynamic_array` - array push, by-ref passing, resize, reserve, move, insert and erase keep the elements in place, and resize rounds capacity up to a power of two from a floor of 16 while reserve stays exact
- `test_subarray` - subarray over a range64 copies exactly the selected elements of a const or a var array, and an empty range64 yields an empty array
- `test_variadic_push_from` - push_from and push_clone_from with two, three or four sources append every source in order into one array
- `test_nested_push_from` - push_from and push_clone_from flatten nested int arrays of any depth into an array of int, while an array-of-arrays target receives the sub-arrays as whole elements
- `test_array_comprehension` - array and table comprehensions, plain and where-filtered, single-line and multiline, in bracket and brace form, produce exactly the mapped elements
- `test_to_array` - to_array over a fixed array, a range iterator, and each of a static or a dynamic array yields the same elements in the same order
- `test_lock_array` - lock and lock_data expose the array's own elements for reading and writing, and an element address taken under lock writes through to the array
- `test_map_to_a` - map_to_array views raw memory as an array of float whose writes land in the underlying uint buffer
- `test_fixed_array_2d` - a two-dimensional global fixed array reads back what was written, is laid out row-major under pointer arithmetic, and prints as nested brackets
- `test_pointer_index` - a pointer indexes the memory it points into with int, uint, int64 and uint64 indices alike
- `test_array_index` - a dynamic array indexes with int, uint, int64 and uint64 indices alike
- `test_fixed_array_index` - a fixed array indexes with int, uint, int64 and uint64 indices alike
- `test_vector_index` - an int3 vector indexes its components with int and uint indices
- `test_table_index` - a table indexes its existing entries by string key and by int key
- `test_struct_pointer_index` - indexing a pointer to int2 elements returns the whole element at that offset
- `test_erase_if_all` - erase_if dropping negatives leaves exactly the non-negative elements, for empty, all-negative and mixed arrays with negative runs at either end and in the middle
- `test_resize_inits` - resize constructs grown struct elements with their field initializers, through the int64 overload too and again after a shrink and regrow, while grown int elements are zero
- `test_resize_and_init` - resize_and_init zeroes trivial elements, fills them with an explicit initial value, and runs the field initializers of a struct element
- `test_sort_all` - sort orders numeric, string, user-operator struct and vector arrays and fixed arrays ascending by default and descending under a comparator, and keeps every element when keys repeat
- `test_stable_sort_all` - stable_sort keeps equal keys in input order across short and long runs, and the bare form sorts arrays, fixed arrays and strings
- `test_any_path_make_pop_heap` - make_heap and pop_heap on a struct array keyed by cmp_by keep the largest key at the root with its payload and pop the keys in descending order
- `test_any_path_push_heap` - push_heap on a struct heap moves a newly pushed largest key to the root together with its payload
- `test_any_path_nth_element` - nth_element on a struct array puts the fifth-smallest key at index 4 with no larger key before it and no smaller key after it
- `test_literal_iterator_elements` - coroutine iterators moved into an array literal arrive live and each runs to completion under cr_run_all
- `test_literal_fixed_array_elements` - fixed arrays returned by calls keep their contents as the elements of an array literal
- `test_ctor_comprehension_move_init` - a comprehension and a moved array passed as struct constructor fields arrive with all their elements
- `test_comprehension_literal_elements` - comprehension elements land intact inside array, tuple and variant literals
- `test_scoped_array_of_arrays_unlocked_after_element_read` - reading an element of a scoped array of arrays between two calls of the function that built it, where that function breaks out of a loop over a temporary array and declares a scoped array in the loop body, leaves the array unlocked for its scoped delete

### assignment_operators.das

- `test_distinct_assign_operator` - a user operator = on a distinct type serves initialization of locals, globals and struct fields as well as assignment, with the distinct type on either side
- `test_same_type_overload_and_raw_forms` - a same-type operator = or := replaces the builtin copy and clone at assignment and at init, while the raw !== and !:= forms stay the builtin ones
- `test_move_operator` - <- dispatches to a user operator <- at init and at assignment, while the raw !<- is the builtin move
- `test_init_reaches_generic_and_mutable_source_overloads` - a generic operator = and one taking a var source serve initialization exactly as they serve assignment
- `test_compiler_made_copies_stay_builtin` - the copies the compiler makes for an inlined return and for a let relocated into finally do not run the user operator = a second time
- `test_every_copy_the_compiler_makes_is_builtin` - a clone init runs only operator :=, and generator locals, ternaries with an inlined arm, returns in a loop with finally and lambda captures run the user operator = at most once
- `test_init_reaches_the_source_by_reference` - a user operator <- taking the source by reference empties a pointer source at init as at assignment, and one taking a const source serves init
- `test_raw_forms_keep_builtin_clones` - the raw !:= reaches the builtin generic clone of an array and the raw !<- accepts a table literal
- `test_more_compiler_made_copies` - the raw move skips a same-type operator <- the plain move takes, inlined two-return results, finally lets after an early out and yielded values run operator = at most once, and an operator from another module serves init and assignment
- `test_init_resolution_matches_assignment` - init picks among two generic operator = overloads by specialization as assignment does, and init from a table read of a type with field defaults runs the operator once
- `test_class_operator` - an operator = declared inside a class takes self as the destination of a dereferenced assignment

### block_annotation_data.das

- `test_block_annotation_data` - the annotation data a block annotation writes in finalize reads back off the runtime block as the expected payload
- `test_annotated_block_still_invokes` - a block carrying annotation data still invokes and returns its body's result
- `test_unannotated_block_has_no_data` - a block with no annotation reports zero annotation data

### blocks_and_lambdas.das

- `test_block_invoke` - a block invokes as a variable, repeatedly, nested inside other blocks over a dirtied stack, and with value, nested and by-reference arguments
- `test_block` - a block held in a local variable returns its result for each invoke
- `test_block_access_function_arg` - a block nested inside a lambda reads the lambda's captured variable
- `test_block_args_nested` - three nested blocks each still see every outer block's argument, by value, by reference, by pointer and as a struct
- `test_block_variable` - a local block variable with or without arguments and with a void, value or struct result reads its captured local when invoked
- `test_block_vs_local_block` - a block passed at the call site and the same block held in a local variable produce the same result
- `test_call_site_block_arrow_body` - a call-site block takes an arrow body in value and move form, beside the braced and <| piped forms
- `test_lambda` - a lambda captures by copy so later writes to the outer variable do not reach it, a default lambda is null, and a returned lambda keeps its capture
- `test_lambda_capture_modes` - capture(& x) shares the outer variable, capture(<- x) moves it out and capture(:= x) clones it, and deleting the lambda finalizes the moved capture once
- `test_lambda_copy_aliases_capture` - copying a lambda aliases its capture frame, so a mutation through one copy is seen through the other

- `test_lambda_struct_field_copy` - copying a struct with a lambda field aliases the lambda, and both copies invoke it

- `test_lambda_to_iter` - a lambda returning bool and writing its reference argument iterates as each(), for an int and for a struct element

### cant_access_private_members.das

compile-fail fixture: reading a private field or calling a private method of a class from outside it does not compile

### cant_addr_cast_non_pointer.das

compile-fail fixture: addr<T>(x) with a non-pointer T does not compile: the target of an address cast must be a pointer type

### cant_addr_cast_unsafe.das

compile-fail fixture: addr<T?>(x) outside unsafe does not compile: it takes an address and reinterprets it, and both gates fire

### cant_delete_super_self.das

compile-fail fixture: delete super.self does not compile without a base class, outside operator delete, or in any other misplaced form

### cant_dereference_mix.das

compile-fail fixture: dereferencing a non-pointer or a void pointer, or ?? with mismatched types, does not compile

### cant_derive_from_sealed_class.das

compile-fail fixture: a class deriving from a sealed class does not compile

### cant_get_field.das

compile-fail fixture: field access on a non-struct type, safe navigation on a non-pointer, and a write through const safe navigation do not compile

### cant_have_local_variable.das

compile-fail fixture: a local variable, array or table of a non-local handled type such as ast::TypeDecl does not compile

### cant_index.das

compile-fail fixture: indexing a value that is not an array or a container does not compile

### cant_intptr_of_scalar.das

compile-fail fixture: intptr of a scalar does not compile: it takes a pointer, smart_ptr, function or lambda, and a scalar carries no address

### cant_override_sealed.das

compile-fail fixture: overriding a sealed field or a sealed method in a derived class does not compile

### cant_raw_clone_with_operator.das

compile-fail fixture: the raw !:= clone of a struct whose operator := is user-defined does not compile: the generated field-wise clone it would fall back to is replaced

### cant_rpipe_into_operator.das

compile-fail fixture: piping a value into an operator does not compile: an operator has no argument list to receive it

### cant_scratch_outside_unsafe.das

compile-fail fixture: every scratch primitive - set_scratch, scratch_reserve, scratch_resize, scratch_ensure_capacity - called outside unsafe does not compile

### cant_unsafe_assign_operator_init.das

compile-fail fixture: an initialization through an [unsafe_operation] operator = outside unsafe does not compile, the same as an assignment through it

### cant_write_generator_for_variable.das

compile-fail fixture: assigning to a for-loop variable inside a generator does not compile: the loop variable is constant

### cant_write_to_constant_value.das

compile-fail fixture: writing a field through a const pointer, directly or through safe navigation, does not compile

### container_finalize.das

- `test_table_banner` - table erase and clear release the heap owned by the dropped values, and erasing a missing key releases nothing
- `test_pointer_carveout` - erase and clear on arrays and tables of borrowed pointers leave the pointees alive
- `test_composite_carveout` - dropping pointer-carrying composite elements skips the release, so their pointees are untouched

### container_init_table.das

- `test_table_index_inits` - indexing a fresh table key runs the value type's field initializers, including an allocating one, before the read, store or var-ref use
- `test_table_index_store_forms` - copy, move, relaxed-assign and clone stores into a fresh table key each land the value without initializing the slot first or leaking its default
- `test_table_index_trivial_unchanged` - fresh table slots of workhorse and container value types still start zero-filled

- `test_postfix_if` - a postfix `return x if (cond)` returns only when its condition holds

- `test_prefix_if_oneliner` - a braceless prefix `if (cond) return x` returns early only when its condition holds

- `test_oneliner_break_continue` - braceless if with break or continue as its body steers the loop
- `test_if_body_on_next_line` - a braceless if body written on the line after the condition parses as that if's body
- `test_else_body_on_next_line` - a braceless else body written on the line after the else parses as the else body
- `test_if_and_else_bodies_on_next_lines` - braceless if and else bodies both on their own next lines pair up correctly
- `test_elif_body_on_next_line` - a braceless elif body on the next line belongs to that elif
- `test_static_if_body_on_next_line` - a braceless static_if body on the next line is kept or dropped by the constant condition
- `test_postfix_if_split_across_lines` - a statement followed by an if on the next line parses as two statements - an unconditional return, then a prefix if - not as a postfix if
- `test_for_const_array` - a for loop over a constant fixed_array literal visits its elements
- `test_continue` - continue skips the rest of the iteration in while, for and zipped for loops
- `test_for_loop` - for loops over fixed arrays, dynamic arrays, ranges, urange and 64-bit ranges, one or two variables, write and read every element, stop at the shorter source, and skip an empty range
- `test_for_single_element_array` - a for loop over a one-element array literal visits that element
- `test_each_ref` - each_ref over a pointer-yielding lambda, and a generator<int&> that lowers to it, iterate genuine references, so writes reach the source array
- `test_loop_ret` - a return from inside a for or while loop leaves the function at once, also when the loop body has a finalized local
- `test_labels` - goto label loops back in plain code, nested ifs, for and while bodies, runs the finally it jumps out of, and a computed goto lands on its numbered label
- `test_a_goto_from_a_loop_body_to_an_outer_label_numbered_below_the_bodys_labels` - a goto from a loop body to an outer label numbered below the body's own labels lands on the outer label
- `test_a_goto_past_a_var_declaration_runs_on_every_tier` - a goto past a var or block-typed let declaration runs on every tier, and the skipped declaration still exists after the label
- `test_a_goto_to_a_label_that_ends_a_block` - a goto to a label that ends a block finishes the block and runs the statement after it
- `test_a_goto_inside_a_block_literal_reaches_its_label` - a static goto inside a block literal reaches the literal's own label, forward or backward, instead of leaving the block
- `test_a_goto_from_a_labelled_block_to_an_outer_label` - a goto from inside a labelled if body to an outer label loops back correctly
- `test_a_computed_goto_into_a_while_body_lands_on_its_label` - a computed goto into a while body lands on the label its runtime value names
- `test_a_computed_goto_resolves_against_the_labels_of_its_own_block` - a computed goto resolves only against the labels of its own function or block literal, never another's
- `test_a_computed_goto_to_a_label_nothing_declares_throws` - a computed goto to a number no label declares raises a recoverable run-time error, also in a global initializer
- `test_if_not_null` - if_not_null calls the piped function with the dereferenced pointer only when the pointer is not null
- `test_bool_condition` - an if over a false bool variable skips its body
- `test_defer` - defer blocks run at scope exit in reverse order, defer_delete deletes at scope exit, and a defer in a bare block inside a lambda fires on each call
- `test_finally` - a finally runs once on an if that breaks, once per iteration of a for or while loop, after a function's return, and after a block
- `test_try_recover_restores_block_arguments` - recovering from a panic raised in a nested block leaves the outer block's argument intact
- `test_try_recover` - try/recover catches a null deref and an explicit panic and runs the recover block
- `test_try_recover_control_flow` - break and continue inside try or recover, nested tries and inner loops leave exactly the loop they name
- `test_try_recover_return` - a return inside a try or recover arm returns the function with its value - an int, a string, a struct returned through memory, a reference, and from a nested try
- `test_with_statement` - a with (struct) block names the struct's fields directly, so assignments inside write them
- `test_loop_without_trailing_return` - a while (true) no reachable break leaves, and a for over non-empty constant ranges whose body returns, need no return after them

### copy_move_and_return.das

- `test_clone` - clone (:=) deep-copies arrays, tables, structs and nested containers, picks a user clone by the source's constness, and clone-initializes variant, tuple and struct fields

- `test_clone_to_move` - clone-initializing an array from another, global or local, copies every element and leaves the source intact

- `test_partial_make_local_return_reads_alias` - a partial struct literal returned beside a returned local zero-fills the fields it omits

- `test_indirect_return_reads_alias` - the other return path reads the returned local's original fields through a reference, a pointer, a block and a global pointer

- `test_string_interpolation_names` - string interpolation prints the value name of uint8, uint16, uint32 and uint64-backed enums whose values exceed the signed range
- `test_sprint_json_unsigned_enum_field` - sprint_json renders an unsigned enum struct field by its value name for every width, top bit set included

### enumerations.das

- `test_enum_conversions` - an enum value interpolates and casts to its name, and to_enum parses a name back, falling back to the given default on an unknown name
- `test_enum_macro_conversions` - [string_to_enum] gives an enum a string constructor, with and without a default, beside the standard to_enum path

- `test_enum_named_like_module_as_field` - an enum named like its own module works as a struct field type

- `test_bitfield_8` - a uint8 bitfield is 1 byte, supports ==, !=, |, &, ^, ~ and their compound forms, converts to and from uint8, and prints each of its 8 named bits
- `test_bitfield_16` - a uint16 bitfield is 2 bytes, supports ==, !=, |, &, ^, ~ and their compound forms, converts to and from uint16, and prints each of its 16 named bits
- `test_bitfield_64` - a uint64 bitfield is 8 bytes, supports ==, !=, |, &, ^, ~ and their compound forms, converts to and from uint64, and prints each of its 64 named bits

### fast_call_depth.das

The recursers live in a no_aot module, so this file runs under AOT and JIT as well: each sweep exercises its own recover handler (the try node, jit_try_recover, das_try_recover). An instrumented run (dastest --cov-path, the debugger) rewrites every body, so nothing is fastcall and the guard counts nothing: the exactness arms skip there, by the probe below.

- `test_fast_call_depth_panics` - fastcall recursion exactly at max_fast_call_depth passes and one call past it panics naming the option, for one, two, computed and nine arguments
- `test_recovered_overflow_leaves_no_drift` - a thousand recovered fastcall overflows leave the depth counter where it was, so a recursion at the cap still passes
- `test_host_policy_and_host_catch` - a host CodeOfPolicies cap limits fastcall depth in a program with no options line, and a host-side catch of the overflow restores the counter

### framed_call_depth.das

The recursers live in a no_aot module, so this file runs under AOT and JIT as well: each sweep exercises its own recover handler (the try node, jit_try_recover, das_try_recover). The simulated stack is sized never to run out before the cap: the cap is the diagnostic under test, `stack overflow while calling` would be the other one.

- `test_call_depth_panics` - framed recursion at the deepest level the cap allows passes and one call past it panics naming the option, for one, two and nine arguments and a struct result
- `test_recovered_overflow_leaves_no_drift` - a thousand recovered framed overflows leave the depth counter where it was, so the probe reaches the same level after them
- `test_host_policy_and_host_catch` - a host CodeOfPolicies cap limits framed call depth in a program with no options line, and a host-side catch of the overflow restores the counter

### functions.das

- `test_unused_may_raise` - an expression whose value is never used still raises its runtime error - index, division, modulo, conversion, user call, user operator, block invoke, assert and verify - instead of being optimized away
- `test_bare_mixed` - a bracket-less call mixes positional and named arguments, several named ones in parameter order, after four positionals
- `test_bracketed_still_works` - the bracketed [name = value] named-argument form still binds
- `test_named_move_clone` - a named argument binds by reference with =, clones with := and moves with <-
- `test_overload_by_named` - the named argument's name and type pick between overloads
- `test_generic_named` - a generic function takes a named argument beside its inferred positional for each instantiation
- `test_piped_block_named` - a piped block fills the block slot of a named call, with a named option before it or defaulted
- `test_method_bare` - a dot method call on a free function takes a positional and a named argument
- `test_method_arrow` - the -> method-call form takes named arguments, bare or bracketed, like the dot form
- `test_method_all_named` - a method call with only named arguments after self resolves through both . and ->
- `test_all_named` - a call with only named arguments resolves as a function call and still picks the overload by name and type
- `test_struct_beats_function` - an all-named call on a name that is both a struct and a function constructs the struct
- `test_class_method_bare` - a genuine class method keeps a middle positional after self beside a named argument, including an implicit-self call
- `test_class_method_arrow` - -> on a genuine class method keeps a middle positional beside a named argument
- `test_class_method_all_named` - a genuine class method called with only named arguments resolves through both . and ->
- `test_named_call_in_generic` - a named call inside a generic body keeps its positional argument when the body is cloned for instantiation
- `test_function_arrow_body` - def name(args) : T => expr and => <- expr parse as function bodies with visibility prefixes, generics, no return type, a body on the next line, and on class and struct methods
- `test_func_addr` - a function pointer invokes, compares to itself and null, and its uint64 handle is the same non-null value in every store position and casts back to a callable, while invoking a null one panics
- `test_nodiscard_in_interpolation` - a [nodiscard] result formatted by string interpolation counts as used, in a call argument and in a let initializer
- `test_nodiscard_consumed_forms` - a [nodiscard] result bound to a let or used as an operand compiles and carries its value

### gen1_syntax.das

- `test_c_character_escapes_lex_in_gen1` - the gen1 lexer reads the C character escapes - bell, vertical tab, hex, octal, quote and question mark - to their code values
- `test_annotation_int64_gen1` - gen1 struct annotations keep full 64-bit signed, unsigned and hex literal arguments, and the int64 minimum literal parses
- `test_annotation_signed_numbers_gen1` - gen1 struct annotations keep negative int and float literal arguments

### generators.das

- `test_generators` - a raw generator yields the right sequence through locals, refs, if/elif, while and for loops with break, continue, nesting and finally, and every range flavor
- `test_generator_block_argument` - a generator body calls a function taking a block literal, read under a loop or twice, and yields its results
- `test_generator_for_source_eval_once` - a for source is evaluated exactly once - in a yielding generator loop, a zip, co_await, yeild_from, a yieldless coroutine and a comprehension
- `test_generator_zip_empty_source` - a generator zipping array or table iterators where one source is empty yields nothing and closes every source cleanly
- `test_typed_coroutine` - a typed [coroutine] yields its values to a for loop counting up, counting down, or not at all
- `test_yielder` - a coroutine of straight-line yields produces exactly those values in order
- `test_cr_run` - cr_run drives a void coroutine through every co_continue to completion
- `test_cr_run_all` - cr_run_all runs several coroutines of different lengths each to completion
- `test_yeild_from` - yeild_from splices a sub-generator's values into the parent's sequence in place
- `test_co_await` - co_await suspends the caller until the awaited coroutine finishes, then resumes it
- `test_generator_unsafe_block_local` - a local declared in an unsafe block of a generator keeps its value across a yield

### generics.das

- `test_partial_specialization` - overload resolution picks the most specialized generic: smallest cast distance, concrete over auto, derived over base, fixed dim, container, pointer, table, tuple and function subtypes
- `test_fully_qualified_generic_name` - a module-qualified call to a bound generic resolves and returns its result, also from inside a function whose result type it infers
- `test_a_generic_over_a_tuple_instantiates_for_void_ptr_after_other_pointers` - a generic over a tuple instantiates for a void? tuple after instances for other pointer tuples
- `test_a_void_ptr_tuple_gets_its_own_instance_after_one_other_pointer` - a void? tuple gets its own generic instance, distinct from the int? tuple instance made before it

- `test_type_alias` - a C++ type alias of float3 (Point3) behaves as float3 in typename, fields, properties, swizzles, arithmetic and aliased arrays
- `test_type_function` - a [type_function] takes a type<T> argument and computes from its size
- `test_option_type` - an option type picks its first matching alternative, so int& | auto binds by reference and auto | int& by value
- `test_logical_ops` - contract annotations combine with !, ||, && and ^^ to gate which generic overload a call picks

- `test_generic_instance_at_the_size_limit` - a generic is instanced with an argument type of exactly 4096 type nodes, the instance size limit

- `test_index_operators_bind_the_concrete_overload` - index-assign operators whose value is a fixed array of an unresolved dimension bind the concrete int[3] overload, not the auto one
- `test_index_assign_on_unresolved_self_binds_the_concrete_overload` - an index assignment into a fixed array of an unresolved dimension binds the concrete int[3] self overload
- `test_index_assign_with_unresolved_index_binds_the_concrete_overload` - an index assignment whose index is a fixed array of an unresolved dimension binds the concrete int[3] index overload
- `test_is_type_on_unresolved_dim` - is type<int[3]> on a fixed array declared with an unresolved dimension answers true once the dimension resolves
- `test_call_with_inferred_argument_binds_the_function` - a call whose argument type is still being inferred - a local, a class member, a field, a method result - binds the intended function, not a same-signature impostor
- `test_method_call_with_inferred_argument_binds_the_function` - a dot method call whose argument comes through nested generic pass-throughs binds the user function over the builtin of the same name
- `test_method_call_on_inferred_receiver_binds_the_function` - a dot method call on a receiver inferred through nested generic pass-throughs binds the user function and leaves the receiver intact
- `test_offsetof_after_unresolved_dim` - typeinfo offsetof of a field after a fixed array with an unresolved dimension counts the resolved size
- `test_pointer_stride_over_unresolved_dim` - pointer + 1, ++ and pointer difference over a struct holding an unresolved-dimension array stride by the resolved struct size
- `test_pointer_stride_over_inferred_field_type` - pointer arithmetic over a struct whose field type is inferred strides by the struct's final size
- `test_pointer_diff_over_inferred_field_type` - the difference of two pointers to a struct with an inferred field type counts elements, not bytes
- `test_pointer_stride_over_self_referential_struct` - pointer + 1 over a self-referential struct strides by the struct's size
- `test_pointer_stride_over_array_of_inferred_struct` - pointer + 1 over a fixed array of structs with an inferred field type strides by the whole array's size
- `test_recursive_result_read_through_a_pending_local` - a recursive function whose result type is read through a local still pending inference infers and returns the right count

### inline_tests.das

- `test_cloned_body_keeps_inferred_state` - an auto-inlined body clone keeps its inferred state: swizzles, constructor calls, field initializers and by-value type witnesses behave as in the call
- `test_splice_lowering` - splices lowered into a conditional move, an &&= right side, a loop and a compiled cross-module callee all compute the call's result
- `test_splice_in_labeled_block` - an [inline] callee with an early return splices correctly at a call between a label and a goto back to it
- `test_discarded_pure_inline_result` - a pure inlined call whose result is discarded, named-argument form included, compiles and leaves the caller's value alone
- `test_no_compile_time_call_of_native_const_ref` - an inlined callee passing a constant-folded argument to a C++-bound const-ref function is not evaluated at compile time and returns the run-time value
- `test_no_capture_when_inlined` - inlining a caller whose argument spells a can_shadow block argument's name does not capture the block's variable
- `test_no_capture_without_can_shadow` - inlining a caller whose argument spells a plain block argument's name renames it, so it compiles and does not capture
- `test_declined_site_keeps_its_statement` - a devirt site that declines on can_shadow capture after hoisting its impure prefix keeps the statement and its temps, and runs the block each time
- `test_inline_shadow_nested_query` - a declined splice keeps a caller's outer reference distinct from a same-named can_shadow block argument nested in its callback, so the shape compiles and runs

### invalid_structure_field_type_void.das
