### invalid_table_type_mix.das

### math_library.das

- `test_vec_swizzle` - swizzles (.xy, .yx, .xyz, .wzyx and the rest) read and write the right components of float, int and uint vectors, also through struct fields
- `test_uint_component_of_value` - a uint component of a returned uint4 stays unsigned through widening, shift, division and printing
- `test_vec_constructors` - float, int, uint and range vector constructors build from components or one splatted scalar, and vector conversions, chained too, keep the component values
- `test_vec_index` - vector [] and ?[] read and write each component, an out-of-range index on either side panics, and arrays of vectors index through
- `test_vec_ops` - vector *= and /= by a scalar match the component-wise scalar result for float, int and uint vectors (skipped on a fast-math host)
- `test_vector_pow_keeps_sign` - vector pow keeps a negative base's sign for odd exponents, while pow_est (GLSL pow) drops it
- `test_horizontal_reduce` - hmin, hmax and hadd reduce float2, float3 and float4 vectors read from the heap to the right scalar
- `test_bit_counting_everything` - clz, ctz and popcnt agree with each other on every single-bit 32 and 64-bit value, and popcnt matches a bit-clearing count on fuzzed values
- `test_random_seeding` - random_seed makes random_int reproducible for one seed and different for two
- `test_random_float_range` - random_float stays in [0, 1)
- `test_random_unit_vector` - random_unit_vector returns vectors of length 1
- `test_random_in_unit_sphere` - random_in_unit_sphere returns points no farther than 1 from the origin
- `test_random_in_unit_disk` - random_in_unit_disk returns points in the unit disk with z = 0
- `test_each_random_uint` - each_random_uint is an endless iterator a for loop can draw from and break out of
- `test_cpu_supports` - cpu_supports reports false for unknown or foreign-architecture names, true for ISA baselines, and keeps the feature implication ladder consistent

### max_unreserved_size.das

- `test_unreserved_resize_panics` - a resize that must grow past max_unreserved_size bytes panics, through resize_no_init and the int64 overload too, with element stride counted
- `test_reserved_and_small_resizes_pass` - reserve-then-resize, small resizes, ensure_capacity appends, zero-stride elements, to_bytes, binary_load, MemSerializer writes and shrinks never trip the unreserved-resize guard
- `test_max_unreserved_size_api` - the max_unreserved_size option, its getter and its runtime setter agree, and lowering the limit again re-arms the guard

### modules.das

- `test_require_as_builtin` - require ... as registers its alias for a builtin C++ module
- `test_require_as_daslib` - require ... as registers its alias for a daslib module
- `test_require_as_same_dir` - a same-directory bare require and its path spelling both register aliases, and the real module name keeps working beside them
- `test_require_as_with_module` - with (module alias) resolves through a require alias while locals stay lexical inside it
- `test_with_module_private_symbols` - inside with (module foo) the block reads and writes foo's private functions, globals, structs, enums and type aliases
- `test_with_module_scoping` - an unqualified name inside with (module foo) resolves in foo while _:: reaches the enclosing module, the innermost nested with wins, a local shadows foo's global, and a generic instantiates inside the block
- `test_class_name_collision_public` - a class named like a class in a publicly required module compiles, and a class derived from that twin gets its own finalizer
- `test_lambda_in_generic_module_vis` - a direct call, a lambda, a generator and a local function inside a generic instance all resolve names from the generic's home module
- `test_private_property_in_module` - a class's private property setter and getter stay callable inside the declaring module, behind public helpers and methods
- `test_access_private_from_lambda` - a lambda created inside a class method reads and writes the class's private fields
- `test_struct_alias_from_two_modules` - a struct and a typedef of it visible from two modules construct through the bare name, the struct's module and the alias's module, with and without fields
- `test_alias_of_enum_handle_and_twin_alias` - a typedef naming a visible enum, a visible handled type, or the same type as another module's typedef is that one candidate, not a second
- `test_alias_of_struct_with_a_twin_name` - a typedef of a struct that shares its name with another visible struct constructs the aliased one, with and without arguments

### operators.das

- `test_operators` - user as, ?as and is operators convert and test a struct, and user [], ?[], . and ?. operators with named property getters answer on a struct and on a class property inherited across required modules
- `test_index_operators` - a struct's [] and [] = method operators read and write single bits of a 64-bit word, and ||=, &&= and ^^= on an element go through them
- `test_raw_operators` - a ! prefix on ., ?., [], ?[], ??, is, as and ?as bypasses the user operator overload and reaches the builtin field, element, coalescing or variant check
- `test_index_move_operator` - the []<- operator in free and method form, and <- through a [] that returns a reference, move the array into the slot and empty the source
- `test_operator_overload` - user unary minus, binary plus and == operators on a struct compose in one expression
- `test_cast` - cast to the base of a derived struct value or pointer lets base-typed code write the derived object's base fields, and reinterpret of a struct reads its bytes as another layout
- `test_cast_binds_tight` - arithmetic after a parenthesized reinterpret applies to the cast pointer at the target element stride, not to the operand
- `test_cast_postfix_applies_outside` - a postfix index after a parenthesized reinterpret applies to the cast result, not to the operand
- `test_div_by_zero` - integer division and modulo by zero raise a recoverable panic for int, uint, int64 and uint64
- `test_shifts` - scalar shifts take the count modulo the bit width, rotations and their compound forms rotate both ways, vector shifts apply per component, and user shift operators on a class accept int and class operands
- `test_setand_and_setor_bool` - ||= and &&= short-circuit like || and && and never evaluate the right side once the result is decided
- `test_safe_index` - ?[] with ?? on arrays, tables, fixed arrays and vectors, directly and through pointers, writes the element when it exists and the fallback when the index misses or the pointer is null
- `test_safe_index_uint` - ?[] with a uint index on arrays, fixed arrays and vectors, directly and through pointers, writes in-range elements and the fallback past the end or through a null pointer
- `test_safe_index_read` - ?[] reads the in-range elements of arrays, fixed arrays, vectors and tables and yields the ?? fallback for a missing index or key
- `test_null_coalescing_const_pointer_const_value` - ?? on a const pointer inside a block returns the pointee when non-null and the block argument when null
- `test_safe_operators` - user [], ?[], . and ?. operators on a struct return the computed value or address on a hit and fall back through ?? on a miss
- `test_rpipe` - |> chains calls left to right and <| supplies the last argument of the same call

### optimization.das

- `test_mul_identities` - folded multiplication identities (x*1, x*0, x*-1 and the like) keep the value and still evaluate an impure operand
- `test_add_sub_identities` - folded addition and subtraction identities (x+0, x-0, x-x and the like) keep the value
- `test_div_mod_identities` - folded division and modulo identities keep the value
- `test_bitwise_identities` - folded bitwise identities (x^x, x&x, x|x and the like) keep the value
- `test_bool_identities` - folded boolean identities keep the value for both values of the variable operand
- `test_ternary_identities` - a folded ternary whose arms are the same expression keeps the value
- `test_same_type_casts` - a folded cast to the operand's own type leaves the value unchanged for every workhorse type
- `test_splat_collapse` - collapsing splat-vector arithmetic keeps the vector result, and splat-with-scalar shapes are left for the vector operator
- `test_dead_loops` - loops the folder removes as dead leave the surrounding values exactly as running them would
- `test_finalizer_only_function_still_runs` - a call to a function whose body is only a finally is kept, so the finally's side effect happens
- `test_cond_fold_keeps_impure_cond` - folding an if whose two arms are equivalent still evaluates its impure condition
- `test_elif_chain_values` - an if/elif return chain folded to nested ternaries returns each branch's value
- `test_cond_fold_keeps_arm_finally` - an if arm holding a return plus a defer is not folded to a ternary return, so the defer still runs
- `test_reassociation_off_by_default` - without fast_math the folder does not regroup float arithmetic chains and their values stay exact
- `test_a_constant_call_into_mutual_recursion_reading_a_global` - a constant-argument call into two mutually recursive functions that read a global is not folded to a compile-time value
- `test_a_constant_call_into_a_three_function_cycle_reading_a_global` - a constant-argument call into a three-function cycle that reads a global is not folded to a compile-time value
- `test_folded_null_pointer_arith` - a ternary guarding pointer arithmetic on a null pointer folds to null instead of an offset pointer
- `test_every_read_of_a_call_result_keeps_the_side_effects_of_the_call` - a call result read through a swizzle, safe field, is, as, ?as, index or safe index still runs the call when the consumer does nothing
- `test_an_addr_argument_keeps_its_side_effects_when_the_call_is_dropped` - an addr() argument whose index has a side effect keeps it once when the empty call is dropped, inline or through a let
- `test_a_field_or_index_argument_keeps_the_side_effects_of_its_base` - a field or vector-index argument keeps the side effect of the call that computes its base or index
- `test_a_store_through_a_pointer_computed_from_an_address_is_a_side_effect` - a store through a pointer computed from an address counts as a side effect, so the function doing it is not optimized away
- `test_a_call_whose_only_effect_is_a_store_through_a_reinterpreted_pointer_is_kept` - a call statement whose only effect is a store through a reinterpreted pointer is kept
- `test_a_nested_inline_call_with_the_callers_var_struct_parameter` - a nested [inline] call that mutates the caller's var struct parameter sees the mutation before the next read
- `inline_generator_preserves_conditional_evaluation` - an [inline] call inside a generator's &&, || or ternary condition keeps short-circuit evaluation
- `test_prefix_global_order` - a global element or scalar read left of a spliced [inline] call that overwrites it reads the value from before the call

### optimization_auto_inline.das

- `test_auto_inline_fired` - a call passing a block literal to a block-taking function splices the callee and devirtualizes the invoke, across multi-exit, struct-result and array-result shapes, and declines recursive callees and element-flavor changes
- `test_auto_inline_behavior` - auto-inlined block-literal calls compute the same values as the calls and evaluate impure arguments once, in call order
- `test_never_inline_block` - a [never_inline] block literal keeps its invoke even though the block-taking callee still inlines
- `test_annotated_block_declines_inline` - a block literal carrying any annotation keeps its invoke, so the annotation's call-site semantics are not spliced away

### optimization_auto_inline_functions.das

- `test_auto_inline_functions_fired` - under auto_inline_functions small loop-free callees, and private callees referenced once regardless of budget, splice at their call sites
- `test_auto_inline_functions_declines` - heuristic auto inlining declines [never_inline], over-budget, looping, recursive, twice-referenced, @@-taken, generic-instance and reference-binding callees, leaving them calls
- `test_auto_inline_macro_fences` - generated finalizers, callers annotated to fence the pass and function-level finally callees stay calls, and a cross-origin generic instance still compiles and runs
- `test_auto_inline_functions_behavior` - auto-inlined and declined calls compute the same results, impure arguments evaluate in call order, and move returns keep their values
- `test_auto_inline_writable_ref_args` - an auto-inlined var parameter binds a reference to a cast, upcast or reinterpret of the argument, and materializes rvalue arguments into a temp before splicing
- `test_auto_inline_writable_ref_args_behavior` - writes through an auto-inlined var parameter reach the caller's variable, and a non-copyable argument is aliased rather than moved out

### optimization_cse.das

- `test_cse_fired` - CSE reuses a pure expression already held by a clean local wherever it is available on every path, and declines after stores to its inputs, on one-arm availability, impure calls, aliased leaves and make-block interiors
- `test_cse_behavior` - functions rewritten by CSE compute the same values, still run both impure calls and recompute an aliased leaf after a store
- `test_const_global_folds_on_the_right_of_a_copy` - a const global with a constant initializer folds to its value on the right of a plain copy, through a pointer store and into a local alike

### optimization_fast_math.das

- `test_fp_zero_folds` - under fast_math x*0 and x-x fold to zero for float and double while an impure operand still runs once
- `test_double_zero_sign_folds` - under fast_math the double x+0, x-0 and 0-x folds give the same values as the unfolded expressions
- `test_reciprocal_division` - under fast_math division by a constant through its reciprocal is exact for powers of two and within tolerance otherwise, for scalars and vectors
- `test_fp_compare_flip` - under fast_math a negated float comparison flips to the opposite comparison with the same result
- `test_reassociation` - under fast_math chained additions and multiplications by constants reassociate into one constant with exact results

### optimization_fold_shape.das

- `test_identity_folds_fired` - algebraic identity folds rewrite the post-optimize AST - x*1, x+0, x*0, double negation, same-type casts, dead loops, splat collapse, x^x - while reassociation stays off without fast_math
- `test_same_as_folds_fired` - folds on structurally identical pure operands - fields, swizzles, index reads, ternary arms - fire, while impure operands and float f - f without fast_math do not fold
- `test_cond_folds_fired` - if/else-return chains fold into ternaries and void arms with a pure condition fold away, while an impure condition or a finally section blocks the fold
- `test_same_as_folds_behavior` - same-shape folds preserve values, and impure same-shape operands still evaluate exactly twice
- `test_function_address_is_not_folded` - a call whose result is built from a function address is not folded into a constant

### optimization_inline.das

- `test_inline_fired` - every direct call to an [inline] function is replaced by its body - expression, multi-statement, generic, multi-return and loop-return bodies alike - binding temps only where an argument needs one
- `test_inline_behavior` - inlined calls compute the same values as calls, evaluating impure arguments once in call order and keeping by-value, by-ref, global-snapshot and finally semantics
- `test_counter_bump` - a cross-module splice of a body carrying interior inline temps keeps their renamed ids, mints its own argument temp and never mints a double underscore
- `test_never_inline_module` - calls into a never_inline module stay calls in every inline tier while the pass stays live elsewhere, and the module's neverInline flag is rtti-visible
- `test_scope_wrapped_inline_fired` - an [inline] callee that uses its module's private symbols still splices, under a generated with (module) wrapper, and so does a call inside a user with (module) block
- `test_scope_wrapped_inline_behavior` - scope-wrapped splices read and write the callee module's private globals, while argument expressions keep resolving at the caller even against a same-named global
- `test_inline_unsafe_fired` - callees with block-form, expression-form or same-module unsafe bodies splice under a generated unsafe wrapper and devirtualize their invokes, while an [unsafe_deref] callee stays a call
- `test_inline_unsafe_behavior` - functions whose inlined callees carry unsafe bodies compute the same values as the calls did

### optimization_inline_operators.das

- `test_inline_operators_fired` - [inline] binary, unary, op-assign and comparison operator overloads splice at their sites, and a small unmarked operator splices through the heuristic tier
- `test_inline_operators_declines` - a [never_inline] operator and an over-budget operator stay regular calls
- `test_inline_operators_behavior` - spliced and declined operator overloads compute the same results, with impure operands evaluated in call order

### optimization_splat_order.das

- `test_splat_swap_declines_when_only_right_is_impure` - the splat-collapse fold declines when only the vector operand has side effects, so the splat reads the scalar before the right operand writes it
- `test_splat_swap_declines_when_only_left_is_impure` - the splat-collapse fold declines when only the splat argument has side effects, so its write lands before the right operand is read
- `test_splat_swap_keeps_evaluation_order` - a splat times a vector with both operands impure evaluates left to right in either operand order

### optional_require.das

- `test_optional_require_guard` - a present plain guard loads its target, and static_if over an absent guard drops its branch before names resolve
- `test_optional_require_path_guard` - a resolvable path guard loads its target, an unresolvable one skips it, and module_exists answers only for modules this module can see
- `test_optional_require_pct_path_guard` - a %/-rooted path guard loads its target when the root is mounted and skips it when the guard file does not resolve
- `test_optional_require_strict_plain_guard` - an absent plain-name guard skips its target even though the target file resolves

### pointers.das

- `test_new_and_fields` - new with named fields or with defaults builds the struct, and field reads and writes through the pointer auto-dereference it
- `test_addr_and_deref` - addr of a local or of a struct field yields a pointer whose * and deref read and write the original variable

- `test_null_pointer` - a default-initialized pointer equals null and the address of a local does not

- `test_pointer_arithmetic` - ++ and += on a pointer advance it over array elements one element per step

- `test_ptr_arithmetic` - pointer ++, --, +=, -=, + and - and indexing step by whole elements for int, int64, uint and uint64 offsets alike, negative signed offsets included
- `test_ptr_index` - a pointer to a fixed array element derefs and indexes every element, and a null default pointer argument takes the ?? fallback without a crash
- `test_ptr_safe_at_int` - ?[] on an int pointer writes and reads the element at the offset when the pointer is non-null and takes the ?? fallback when it is null

- `test_ptr_safe_at_int64_index` - ?[] on a pointer with an int64 index reads the element when non-null and the ?? fallback when null
- `test_ptr_safe_at_uint64_index` - ?[] on a pointer with a uint64 index reads the element when non-null and the ?? fallback when null
- `test_ptr_safe_at_struct` - ?[] on a struct pointer returns the whole element when non-null and the fallback struct when null
- `test_ptr_safe_at_ptr_to_ptr` - ?[] on a pointer to pointers returns the stored pointer when non-null and the null fallback when null
- `test_deref_ptr_fun` - deref of a pointer returned by a bound C++ function prints its pointee inside string interpolation
- `test_addr_cast_basic` - addr<float?> of a float3 reinterprets its address, so indexing the result reads the components

- `test_addr_cast_exact_type` - addr<int?> of an int is a plain addr whose writes reach the variable
- `test_addr_cast_self_delimiting` - a postfix index after addr<T?>(x) applies to the cast pointer, not to x
- `test_offset_pointer_write_through_helper` - a callee writing its output pointer only through a helper called with an offset pointer keeps the write, exactly like a direct write or an unoffset helper call
- `test_reinterpret_of_an_extern_uint64_result` - reinterpret to a pointer of an extern call's uint64 result agrees whether applied directly or through a local
- `test_reinterpret_of_an_extern_pointer_result` - reinterpreting two pointers to integers and subtracting gives their byte offset, inline in a generic and through a local alike
- `test_ignore_deref` - a class pointer copied out of an array, by inferred type or by explicit pointer type, stays callable with ->
- `test_smart_ptr` - smart_ptr use counts rise on := and fall on delete with the object freed at zero, a move transfers ownership, a raw pointer reinterpreted back to smart_ptr frees the object, and ?. with ?? reads and writes through it
- `test_mksmart_zero` - the default value of a smart_ptr type, returned by move, holds a null pointer
- `test_memset` - memset8, memset16, memset32, memset64 and memset128 fill exactly the counted elements from the start address and leave the rest zero
- `test_memmove` - memmove copies an overlapping range in both directions with an int, uint, int64 or uint64 size, and copies between distinct buffers
- `test_memzero` - memzero clears a scalar and every element of a fixed array
- `test_const_strip_write_through_passthrough` - a write through a const-stripped pointer parameter stays a side effect when the pointer reaches it through one or two const pass-throughs or let aliases, so every forwarding call keeps the write

- `test_dollar_module` - walking every enum, struct, annotation, function, generic and global of the builtin $ module completes without a crash

- `test_registered_modules_safe` - every registered module's enums, structs, annotations, functions and globals can be walked without a crash

### scratch_containers.das

- `test_scratch_reserve` - scratch_reserve sets capacity to exactly the asked size, for the int and int64 overloads, and leaves length zero

### scratch_very_safe.das

- `test_scratch_eager_vs_deferred` - under very_safe_context a scratch-marked array frees each old buffer on growth, an unmarked one keeps every generation live, and set_scratch(false) restores the deferral
- `test_scratch_reserve_forces_eager` - scratch_reserve frees the old buffer eagerly whether or not the scratch bit is set, and leaves the bit unset

- `test_scratch_table` - under very_safe_context a scratch-marked table frees old blocks at each rehash and keeps the bit through every rehash, an unmarked one retains them, and delete clears the bit

## linq/

### failed_linq_das.das

compile-fail fixture: Malformed %linq! queries (bad keywords, ill-formed group/join/multiple-from/correlated-from clauses) must not compile: each emits exactly one macro error 50503.

### failed_linq_das_table.das

compile-fail fixture: A linq_das query over a table source with a typed range variable, or over a table with a non-copyable value type, must not compile (errors 50503 and 31400).

### failed_test_linq_join.das

compile-fail fixture: _join and _left_join with a non-equi-join on predicate (theta or AND-chained multi-key) must not compile: each shape emits macro error 50503.

### uncategorized_no_aot.das

The audio system a program created survives a reload, a full reload and a reset under the live host: the program's shutdown() leaves it up (audio_live_keeps_handles), audio_live carries the handles over with the old context's reference, and the next init() pushes through them; the real shutdown finalizes it once. None of it throws, and nothing is left in the job-status census the host prints at exit.

- `test_audio_survives_reloads` - two reloads, a full reload and a reset keep the audio system up in a spawned daslang-live host, and /shutdown leaves nothing behind
- `test_host_serves_status` - a spawned daslang-live host answers /status within the ready budget and /shutdown ends it with exit code 0

## lsp/

### uncategorized.das

Protocol tests for the LSP front (utils/watchdog/lsp_front.das, `watchdog --lsp`), driven over a stdio pipe through both hosts (precedent: tests/mcp/test_popen_argv_pipe.das). One live session covers: initialize handshake, didOpen with broken buffer text while the disk file stays clean (publishDiagnostics must reflect the buffer — the --overlay path), didChange back to clean (empty publish), a definition request, the call-hierarchy loop (prepare -> incomingCalls with the item's data round-tripped verbatim -> outgoingCalls from the returned caller item), an implementation request (base method -> derived override), hover / definition / references on declarations (a class name, its parent, a user finalizer, a lambda's argument and capture, a for loop variable), and shutdown/exit. Every frame header is checked byte-exact.

- `test_lsp_protocol` - a full LSP session over a pipe works end to end on every front host, and the validated file record lands in the workspace module cache
- `test_validate_project_root` - with -project_root the consumer validates clean, and without it the same file reports the require it cannot resolve

### failed_match_unreachable_exhausted_variant.das

### test_match_arms.das

- `test_alternative_call_patterns` - An alternative written as a call matches its value against the argument, wins over a same-named function, and match_expr calls the function
- `test_legacy_if_arms_still_compile` - Legacy if-style match arms still compile and select the right arm
- `test_ranges_and_constants_that_touch_but_do_not_overlap` - A range and constants that touch without overlapping pick the right arm at every boundary
- `test_match_value_block_body` - A return in an arm's block body is the arm's value and leaves only that arm
- `test_static_match_keeps_arms_other_instances_need` - A static match instance keeps an arm unreachable for it but needed by another instance

### test_match_arrow.das

- `test_several_values` - A match on several values at once picks the arm whose every column fits
- `test_several_values_of_different_types` - A match may take scrutinees of different types (struct, enum, variant) in one arm list
- `test_int_alternation_is_not_folded` - An integer alternation arm still matches each of its values after lowering
- `test_guard_keeps_bitwise_or` - A guard that uses bitwise or is kept as an expression and not read as an alternation
- `test_bare_name_binds_instead_of_comparing` - A bare name in a pattern binds the value and does not compare against an outer variable of that name
- `test_match_expr_compares_a_variable` - match_expr compares the scrutinee against a variable's value
- `test_bool_patterns` - Boolean patterns across two columns select the right arm for all four combinations
- `test_value_in_let` - A match used as a let initializer yields the arm's value
- `test_value_as_argument` - A match used as a call argument yields the arm's value
- `test_value_inside_statement_arm` - A value match nested inside a statement arm yields its own arm's value
- `test_assignment_bodies` - Arms whose bodies are assignments update the accumulators they name
- `test_static_match_arrow_arms` - A generic static match keeps the arrow arms that fit each instance's type
- `test_value_takes_declared_result_type` - A value match takes the declared result type, so arms of derived class types convert to the base pointer
- `test_scrutinee_is_evaluated_once` - The scrutinee expression is evaluated exactly once, in both value and statement form
- `test_lvalue_scrutinee_is_evaluated_once` - An l-value scrutinee's index expression is evaluated once even when an arm writes through it
- `test_exhaustive_value_match_needs_no_catch_all` - A value match that covers every case compiles without a catch-all arm and picks the right arm
- `test_complementary_guards_cover_their_pattern` - Complementary guards count as covering their pattern, so no catch-all arm is needed
- `test_and_pattern_binds_the_whole_value` - An and pattern binds the whole value alongside its parts
- `test_struct_fields_are_checked_for_coverage` - Struct field patterns are checked column by column for coverage and select the right arm
- `test_range_patterns_are_half_open` - Range patterns include their low end and exclude their high end
- `test_alternatives_may_bind_different_places` - The alternatives of an or pattern may bind the same name from different places
- `test_table_patterns` - Table patterns match keys and key-value pairs and let an arm update the matched table
- `test_view_patterns` - View patterns read array and string contents in place for arms over arrays, fields and tuples
- `test_view_reads_the_value_where_it_stands` - A view pattern reads the value where it stands, across variant alternatives and tuple columns
- `test_view_result_matches_a_variant_alternative` - A view call's result can be matched against a variant alternative
- `test_variant_alternative_called_by_name` - A variant alternative written as a call matches on its value, top level or in a field
- `test_variant_case_without_value_called_by_name` - A value-less variant case written as a call matches by name
- `test_string_prefix_and_suffix_patterns` - String prefix and suffix patterns match and bind the remaining parts

### test_match_solver.das

- `test_solve_coverage` - The coverage solver reports unreachable arms and the missing values of finite and open columns
- `test_solve_coverage_guards` - Guards cover a pattern only when their outcomes are complete questions about the same fact
- `test_overlaps` - Key, span and any cells overlap exactly when they share a value, and rows overlap only when every column does
- `test_all_of` - all_of intersects cells as sets, and disjoint cells intersect to nothing
- `test_questions` - The solver's reachability, exhaustiveness, overlap and missing-value questions answer correctly
- `test_unsupported_facts` - The exact backend names the arm whose fact it cannot decide, and decidable facts raise no error

### uncategorized.das

- `test_all_match` - Every match form (enum, struct, variant, array, tuple, or, pointer, AST and is/as patterns) selects the right arm
- `test_match_edge_cases` - Edge-case match shapes (nested, empty, spread, tail literal, or, guards) select the right arm
- `test_every_match_of_a_function_keeps_its_place` - Each match of a function keeps its own site, so typed lets, nested matches and statement matches do not mix
- `test_match_ast_node_bind` - The ampersand form binds an AST node at the class the pattern tests
- `test_r2v_peel` - A class pattern peels a ref-to-value wrapper, while an explicit wrapper pattern matches the wrapper itself

### uncategorized_no_aot.das

a variant with no name of its own is spelled ``variant`` in a coverage error - never the alias of one of its alternatives' types, which ``describe`` prints after the first ``aka``

- `test_unaliased_variant_is_spelled_variant` - A non-exhaustive match on an unaliased variant spells the missing case with the word variant

### uncategorized_no_aot_rtti.das

- `test_bound_name_inside_reification_tag` - A name bound by a match arm can be used inside a reification tag

## mcp/

### test_mcp_jsonrpc.das

Subprocess-level smoke tests for the MCP server. Spawns ``daslang.exe utils/mcp/main.das`` via ``popen_argv_pipe`` and exercises the JSON-RPC wire — verifies framing, protocol shape, and tool dispatch end-to-end (not just the in-process dispatch table).

- `test_initialize` - an MCP initialize request is answered with serverInfo.name daslang and the session exits with 0
- `test_tools_list_non_empty` - tools/list returns a non-empty tools array
- `test_tools_call_list_modules` - tools/call for list_modules returns non-empty content
- `test_method_not_found` - an unknown MCP method is answered with a JSON-RPC error

### test_popen_argv_pipe.das

Unit tests for the ``popen_argv_pipe`` C++ builtin (bidirectional subprocess pipe). Validates the round-trip semantics that the MCP subprocess tests depend on, isolated from MCP itself.

- `test_echo_roundtrip` - popen_argv_pipe round-trips writes and reads through the pipe of an echo child
- `test_exit_code_propagated` - popen_argv_pipe returns the exit code of the child process
- `test_stdin_eof_after_block` - closing stdin at the end of the popen_argv_pipe block lets the echo child exit cleanly

## metal/

### test_metal_arith.das

- `test_uarith_gpu_vs_cpu` - uint arithmetic run on the GPU gives the same results as the CPU reference.
- `test_iarith_gpu_vs_cpu` - int arithmetic run on the GPU gives the same results as the CPU reference.
- `test_farith_gpu_vs_cpu` - float arithmetic including fmod run on the GPU matches the CPU reference within tolerance.
- `test_vecarith_gpu_vs_cpu` - Vector arithmetic and all/any compares run on the GPU match the CPU reference within tolerance.
- `test_math_gpu_vs_cpu` - Math builtins run on the GPU with precise math match the CPU reference within tolerance.
- `test_mul_ab_gpu_vs_cpu` - The emitted MSL of a*b run on the GPU equals a CPU run of the same method.

### test_metal_control.das

- `test_control_gpu_vs_cpu` - Control-flow kernels run on the GPU give the same results as the CPU reference.
- `test_loops_gpu_vs_cpu` - Loops with a bounds guard on a non-exact grid match the CPU reference and leave the sentinel padding untouched.
- `test_grid_ids_gpu_vs_cpu` - The workgroup-grid builtins read on the GPU equal a CPU replay of the grid.

### test_metal_functions.das

- `test_functions_gpu_vs_cpu` - A chain of user functions emitted to MSL gives on the GPU the same results as the CPU run of the same method.
- `test_threadgroup_param_gpu` - A writable threadgroup-slab parameter with a barrier inside a helper gives the right group sums.
- `test_pointer_param_gpu` - Device and threadgroup pointer parameters give the right advancing dot product and slab maximum.
- `test_class_gpu_vs_cpu` - Class methods with inheritance devirtualized on the GPU equal the CPU vtable run.
- `test_uniform_struct_gpu_vs_cpu` - A kargs uniform struct passed to the GPU gives the same results as the CPU run of the same method.
- `test_state_members_gpu_vs_cpu` - Per-thread state members on the GPU equal a fresh CPU instance per lane.
- `test_consttab_gpu_vs_cpu` - Hoisted constant tables give the same results on the GPU as the CPU reference.

### test_metal_lattice.das

- `test_halfarith_gpu_vs_cpu` - fp16 arithmetic with fastmath off is bit-exact between the GPU and the CPU reference.
- `test_latconv_gpu_vs_cpu` - Int-lattice converts, saturation and fp16 converts on the GPU equal the CPU reference.
- `test_packed3_gpu_vs_cpu` - Packed three-lane buffers with the daslang strides read and write the same on the GPU as the CPU reference.
- `test_sdot_gpu_vs_cpu` - sdot4 and usdot4 lower to their helpers and the GPU result is exactly the CPU reference.

### test_metal_plumbing.das

- `test_host_plumbing` - The pipeline cache, buffer pool and multi-dispatch encoder work together.
- `test_residency_heartbeat` - The residency heartbeat arms, witnesses and unregisters on release, and the submit trace branch runs.
- `test_pool_release_null_guard` - pool_release refuses a null buffer instead of letting it surface later as an unrelated bind.
- `test_buffer_release_returns_memory` - A released buffer's pages leave the process footprint.
- `test_pool_bucket` - pool_bucket returns at least 256 and the next power of two above the request.

### test_metal_sgmat.das

- `test_sgmat_gpu_vs_cpu` - A single simdgroup_matrix tile on the GPU is bit-exact with the CPU replay.
- `test_sgmat_rolled_gpu_vs_cpu` - A rolled GEMM with matrix arrays under unroll_full is bit-exact with a direct CPU matmul.
- `test_sgmat_tiled_gpu_vs_cpu` - A tiled simdgroup_matrix GEMM is bit-exact with a direct CPU matmul.

### test_metal_simd.das

- `test_simd_gpu_vs_reported_membership` - A simdgroup sum and shuffles on the GPU equal values recomputed from the reported simdgroup membership.
- `test_atomic_add_gpu_vs_cpu` - Atomic adds into a threadgroup histogram and a device counter give the CPU-computed totals.
- `test_reduce_gpu_vs_cpu` - A threadgroup tree reduction yields partials equal to the directly computed sums.
- `test_subgroup_ids_shared` - The gl_Subgroup* builtins resolve once across the metal and spirv builtin modules.

### test_metal_tensor_ops.das

- `test_tensor_ops` - tmm2d lowering generates the helpers and the MPP preamble, and the GPU result equals the CPU replay exactly.
- `test_tmm2d_bk_shapes` - tmm2d with bk 64 and 128 across the K sweep and the 72-half deva tile is exactly the CPU replay.
- `test_tmm2d_rx` - tmm2d rx with a register-filled left operand against a device half table matches the reference regardless of layout.
- `test_tmm2d_tile_tg_replay` - The tmm2d_tile_tg CPU replay is the tile product and the scratch's old contents are gone.
- `test_tmm2d_devab` - tmm2d devab and devabnt over two device-half steps at kk 40 and 8 with ldb 56 equal the CPU replay exactly.

## module_cache/

### test_content_key.das

- `test_module_edit_inside_its_stamp` - A same-stamp edit to a module is caught by content and the warm run serves the new text
- `test_included_file_edit_inside_its_stamp` - A same-stamp edit to an included file is caught by content and the warm run serves the new text
- `test_included_stamps_survive_writeback` - The included files' stamps survive a cache writeback, so the next run still serves clean
- `test_included_source_count_bound` - A driver with 4095 included files round-trips through the cache, and one more include makes the read fail and fall back to a rewrite
- `test_writer_temp_is_private` - A cold run still writes its record when the shared temporary name is already taken, so the writer uses a private temporary

### test_default_cache_path.das

an AOT-consuming host (`test_aot --use-aot`) installs no default cache, and spawned as a child it runs the AOT'd program, not the script - no cache marker ever prints; the cell skips there

- `test_fallback_verdict_names_the_cutoff` - An explicit -module-cache reports how many modules it served and which module was the cutoff
- `test_policy_change_refuses_the_cache` - A record written under one set of compile policies serves nothing to a compile under another
- `test_source_stamp_is_content` - The record stamps a module's file by content, so a byte-identical rewrite serves and a same-size edit is a cutoff
- `test_source_derived_syntax_policy_serves` - A gen2 module is served by a -v1syntax host and does not rewrite the cache every run
- `test_aot_generation_reads_cached_modules` - A deserialized module still reads as AOT-capable, so the AOT generator emits non-empty stubs
- `test_source_lines_survive_the_cache` - A served module keeps its source lines, so lint nolint markers still apply on a warm run
- `test_default_module_cache` - The module cache is on by default, silent and keyed by script, host flags and environment, and the flags that turn it off or make it loud work
- `test_default_cache_evicts_to_the_limit` - The default cache directory holds at most DAS_MODULE_CACHE_LIMIT megabytes, evicts oldest records first, keeps the one just written and never prunes an explicit path

### test_macro_cache.das

a module whose compile registered a call macro into itself (an annotation's apply) is never served from the cache: the record replays the module's init, not that registration, so the reader reparses it in place while the records around it still serve (src/ast/ARCHITECTURE.md#module-cache-read)

- `test_apply_macro_reparse` - A module whose compile registered a call macro into itself is never served from the cache and is reparsed in place while the records around it still serve
- `test_extern_registrar_reparse` - A module whose compile registered an extern proxy into dasbind is never served from the cache and reparses in place while the driver still serves
- `test_extern_between_registrars_served` - A module compiled between two dasbind registrars is served from the cache and the cache is not rewritten
- `test_macro_dep_invalidate` - The module cache gates a macro-registered file input by content, not mtime, so a rewritten identical sidecar keeps serving and a changed one invalidates
- `test_a_same_module_call_macro_in_a_generic_body_writes_to_the_cache` - A cold run with a same-module call macro in a generic body writes its record and the warm run reparses the script
- `test_a_script_that_requires_a_marked_module_writes_its_record` - A script that requires a marked module still writes its own record because the marked module is a reference in it

### test_module_loading.das

- `test_member_module_name` - A group member's module name is its last path segment, less the .das a relative spelling carries
- `test_module_groups` - require [group] over a project root expands to its members, reports an unused group by name and stamps the expansion into the cache
- `test_require_module_now` - A late require compiles a shared module at the call, answers the same module afterwards, and answers null with the reason for an absent, unshared, broken or misnamed one
- `test_require_module_now_children` - A late require keeps its own cache file and a call from a running script panics, as a child process shows
- `test_deferred_modules` - A replayed dm row is not loaded by the scan, a deferred module loads on demand, and the cache, artifact and fallback arms behave across cold and warm starts
- `test_descriptor_manifest` - The manifest beside each .das_module records and replays descriptors, keeps binary kinds and targets apart, rejects bad manifests and survives opt-out and write failures
- `test_late_require_keeps_global_offsets` - A module required late from an init keeps the global offsets of the variables around it

### uncategorized.das

- `annotation64_cache_roundtrip` - A module with a 64-bit annotation argument writes its record on the cold run and serves clean from the cache on the warm run
- `test_builtin_embedded_not_cached` - A builtin module's embedded source compiles with the stream hidden, so its hash is the same cold and warm and the program serves clean
- `test_compile_file_module_cache` - compile_file under module_cache writes on a cold compile, serves every module warm, reparses an edited module and compiles from source with the policy off
- `test_generic_instance_origin` - A generic instance restored from the cache keeps its origin generic, so the warm run compiles as the cold one does
- `test_no_optimizations_keeps_shared_dependencies_private` - A compile with optimizations off does not promote the shared module it compiled, while an optimizing compile does and a later unoptimized compile reuses that copy
- `test_shared_typename_cache` - A compound type name in a shared module reads the same on a cold run and on a warm run served clean from the cache
- `test_type_backref_stays_in_module_record` - A main-module type equal to one in a shared module's record never reaches the throwaway copy through the stream's type table

### uncategorized_no_aot.das

- `test_served_module_keeps_shared_types` - A module read back from a serialized program keeps the type sharing its compile left and is marked as read from the cache
- `test_rtti_serializer_round_trip` - The rtti serializer round-trips a whole program in process and its read timers account for the read

### test_msl_arith.das

- `test_iarith_shape` - int arithmetic and unary negate emit the expected MSL and match the golden snapshot.
- `test_farith_shape` - float arithmetic emits the expected MSL with % lowering to fmod and matches the golden snapshot.
- `test_vecarith_shape` - Componentwise vector arithmetic, scalar broadcast and all/any compares emit the expected MSL and match the golden snapshot.
- `test_mathcalls_shape` - Unary float math, vector and integer math classes, round and the f32/i8 converts lower by name and match the golden snapshot.

### test_msl_control.das

- `test_control_shape` - Locals, if/elif/else chains, compound assignment, increment and decrement, comparisons, logical operators and ternaries emit the expected MSL.
- `test_control_golden` - The control-flow kernel's emitted MSL matches its golden snapshot.
- `test_loops_shape` - A @uniform scalar parameter, a bounds guard, while with break and continue, and the range-for forms emit the expected loop MSL.
- `test_loops_golden` - The loops kernel's emitted MSL matches its golden snapshot.

### test_msl_functions.das

- `test_msl_functions` - User functions lower 1:1 with signatures, address spaces and hidden builtins, generic instances get distinct names, and class methods flatten inline.
- `test_msl_state_and_naming` - Thread-local fixed arrays and mutable-pointee riders emit as state, and an absent name= derives the companion names and a qualified entry point.
- `test_msl_const_tables` - Literal fixed-array locals hoist to program-scope constant tables.
- `test_msl_template_call` - A [template] instance lowers to MSL and is called by its base name.
- `test_msl_uniform_struct` - A @uniform struct lowers to one constant& parameter plus a preamble struct.
- `test_msl_shape_stays_literal` - A per-type overload keeps the shape constant literal in the emitted text.

### test_msl_lattice.das

- `test_halfarith_shape` - fp16 closed arithmetic, h literals and all/any compares emit native half MSL and match the golden snapshot.
- `test_latconv_shape` - Int-lattice storage and converts emit clamp-based saturating narrows and match the golden snapshot.
- `test_packed3_shape` - Three-lane elements take packed_T3 with wrapped loads and whole-element stores and match the golden snapshot.

### test_msl_sgmat.das

- `test_sgmat_shape` - Simdgroup matrix locals, loads, stores, multiply and multiply-accumulate lower to simdgroup types, including the tiled threadgroup staging and the store into a workgroup slab.
- `test_sgmat_rolled_shape` - Arrays of simdgroup tiles under unroll_full keep their loops rolled.
- `test_sgmat_golden` - The sgmat, tiled and rolled kernels' emitted MSL match their golden snapshots.
- `test_mul_ab_shape` - The mul_ab kernel emits the expected signature, body statements and companion globals.
- `test_mul_ab_golden` - The mul_ab kernel's emitted MSL matches its golden snapshot.

### test_msl_simd.das

- `test_simd_shape` - Simdgroup builtin parameters and the per-scalar-class intrinsic calls emit the expected MSL.
- `test_simd_golden` - The simd kernel's emitted MSL matches its golden snapshot.
- `test_threadgroup_shape` - @workgroup members become body-top threadgroup declarations, barriers lower, and the workgroup-grid builtins become parameters.
- `test_threadgroup_golden` - The threadgroup reduce kernel's emitted MSL matches its golden snapshot.

### test_msl_tensor_ops.das

- `test_tmm2d_device_forms` - The tensor matmul device forms pick one helper per operand-type pair, name the q8 bk helpers distinctly, and pad staged rows per bk.
- `test_tmm2d_staged_protocol` - The staged tensor protocol makes the acc local the cooperative tensor, types the operand tensor from the begin witness, and stages B natural or transposed per form.

### test_option.das

- `test_constructors` - some carries its value, none is empty for its named type, is_some and is_none agree and different payload types work
- `test_map` - map transforms a some, leaves none as none and can change the payload type
- `test_filter` - filter keeps a matching some, drops a non-matching one and passes none through
- `test_and_then` - and_then chains some to some, short-circuits on none and can return none
- `test_or_else` - or_else passes a some through and runs the fallback on none
- `test_or_value` - or_value passes a some through and substitutes a value on none
- `test_unwrap` - unwrap, unwrap_or, unwrap_or_else, unwrap_or_default and move_unwrap return the payload or the fallback as specified
- `test_operators` - the ?? operator unwraps or defaults and == and != compare options with options and with payload values
- `test_if_some_if_none` - if_some and if_none run their block only on the matching state
- `test_zip` - zip of two somes is a some pair and either none makes the result none
- `test_chaining` - a some flows through map, filter and unwrap_or while a none short-circuits the whole chain
- `option_brittle_constructors` - an Option of a struct with must-init fields compiles as none, as a bare var and as a some that round-trips
- `option_brittle_unwrap_or_default` - unwrap_or_default of a none Option of a must-init struct returns the struct's defaults

- `test_and_then` - and_then chains an Option of an array and short-circuits on none

- `test_if_some_if_none` - if_some and if_none run their block with the array only on the matching state
- `test_equality` - == on an Option of an array compares the arrays
- `test_chaining` - a some array flows through map, filter and unwrap_or while a none short-circuits
- `test_zip` - zip of two some arrays yields a pair of arrays and either none makes the result none
- `test_op_qq` - the ?? operator unwraps a some array and returns the fallback on none
- `test_op_eq_value` - an Option of an array compares with == and != against a plain array

- `test_if_ok_if_err` - if_ok and if_err run their block only on the matching state

### failed_in_array_literal.das

- `test_soa_to_array` - to_array converts the SOA back to an array and from_array then to_array round-trips the data

### test_soa_iteration.das

- `test_soa_for_loop_basic` - a for loop over an SOA visits every element with the right field values
- `test_soa_for_loop_entity` - a for loop over an entity SOA reads its int, string and bool fields
- `test_soa_for_loop_mixed` - an SOA loop combines with a count or range iterator
- `test_soa_for_loop_after_erase` - a for loop after an erase visits the remaining elements
- `test_soa_for_loop_single_field_access` - a for loop that touches only one field of a particle reads the right values

### test_soa_noncopyable.das

- `test_noncopyable_push_preserves_source` - pushing a named variable with a non-copyable field leaves the source intact
- `test_noncopyable_push_and_access` - a push by move with an array field works with indexed access to every field
- `test_noncopyable_iteration` - a for loop over an SOA with an array field reads the array and the other fields
- `test_noncopyable_erase` - erase removes an element that has an array field
- `test_noncopyable_pop` - pop removes the last element that has an array field
- `test_noncopyable_clear` - clear removes all elements that have array fields
- `test_noncopyable_resize` - resize truncates array fields when shrinking and extends with defaults when growing
- `test_noncopyable_reserve` - reserve leaves the length of an SOA with array fields unchanged
- `test_noncopyable_capacity` - capacity works on a struct with an array field
- `test_noncopyable_swap` - swap exchanges elements that have array fields and is a no-op for the same index
- `test_noncopyable_push_clone` - push_clone clones a non-copyable field and does not consume the source
- `test_noncopyable_modify_array_field` - an array field can be modified, cleared and changed in a loop through the SOA
- `test_noncopyable_from_array` - from_array clones non-copyable fields and preserves the source array
- `test_noncopyable_to_array` - to_array clones non-copyable fields and round-trips the data

## spirv/

### test_arith.das

- `test_uint_arith` - uint arithmetic lowers to IAdd, ISub, IMul, UDiv and UMod.
- `test_int_arith` - int arithmetic lowers to SDiv, SRem, SNegate and Not.
- `test_float_arith` - float arithmetic lowers to FAdd, FSub, FMul, FDiv, FRem and FNegate.
- `test_bitwise` - Bitwise &, |, ^, << and >> lower to BitwiseAnd, Or, Xor and shifts, with >> split by signedness.
- `test_bit_cast` - int, uint and float bit-casts lower to OpBitcast and the cast body is never emitted.
- `test_scalar_conversions` - float, int and uint casts lower to the matching OpConvert and OpBitcast opcodes.
- `test_bool_const` - false and true lower to OpConstantFalse and OpConstantTrue with an OpTypeBool.
- `test_emit_type` - emit_type produces the expected type instructions and deduplicates repeated types.

### test_compute.das

- `test_shared_and_barriers` - A compute kernel using @workgroup memory, barrier, memoryBarrierShared and atomicAdd emits the shared-memory, barrier and atomic opcodes and passes spirv-val.
- `test_buffer_barrier` - memoryBarrierBuffer followed by barrier in a compute kernel emits the buffer-scope memory barrier for the cross-invocation SSBO handoff.
- `test_atomic_family` - The atomic family on shared int and uint counters lowers to the matching Op Atomic opcodes and validates.
- `test_square_opcodes` - The compute square kernel emits the expected load, multiply and store opcode shape.
- `test_square_validates` - The compute square kernel's module is accepted by spirv-val.
- `test_workgroup_size_is_a_decorated_constant` - gl_WorkGroupSize lowers to a WorkgroupSize-decorated OpConstantComposite.

### test_control.das

- `test_uint_control` - uint control flow (var, compound assignment, ++, compare, logical, if-else) lowers and validates.
- `test_int_control` - Signed int comparisons in control flow lower to the signed compare opcodes.
- `test_float_control` - Float comparisons in control flow lower to the ordered compare opcodes.
- `test_ternary_select` - cond ? a : b lowers to OpSelect for scalars and vectors.
- `test_ternary_lazy_operand` - A ternary, && or || with an SSBO load in an operand becomes a branch while pure operands stay OpSelect.

### test_coopmat.das

- `test_coopmat` - Cooperative-matrix tiles (f16 GEMM, int8, f32 accumulator with convert, workgroup-memory load, accumulator arrays under unroll_full) emit the KHR coopmat opcodes, capabilities and SPIR-V 1.6 floor.
- `test_coopmat2` - A cm2 q8 GEMM with decode-in-load emits tensor addressing, the decode function and workgroup-scope tiles.
- `test_coopmat2_cls` - A cm2 decode method on a kernel class emits a self-erased signature with member access and l-tile shapes.
- `test_coopmat2_decode_vector_synth` - A synthesized vector decode twin declares its capability and extension, sets both mask bits, serves two loads with one twin and makes four calls of the scalar body.
- `test_coopmat2_decode_vector_scalar_only` - A scalar-only decode load declares no vector capability or extension and emits DecodeFunc alone in two functions.
- `test_coopmat2_decode_vector_free` - A hand-laid vector twin written as a free function returns half4, sets both mask bits and synthesizes no calls.
- `test_coopmat2_decode_vector_hand` - A hand-laid vector twin written as a class method returns half4, sets both mask bits and synthesizes no calls.
- `test_coopmat2_decode_vector_strip` - strip_decode_vector turns a vector-decode module into a scalar-only one and leaves foreign word streams intact.
- `test_coopmat2_e_tiles` - The cm2 e-stamp tile shapes (A 128x32, B 32x128, f16 and f32 128x128 accumulators) build through the name-parsed marker rail.
- `test_coopmat2_fa` - A cm2 flash-attention kernel emits the reduce and per-element callbacks, the use conversion and tile algebra.
- `test_coopmat2_fa256_tiles` - The cm2 h256 flash tile shapes build through the name-parsed marker rail.
- `test_coopmat2_fa512_tiles` - The cm2 h512 flash tile shapes in f32 and f16 build through the name-parsed marker rail.
- `test_coopmat2_h96` - The cm2 head-96 flash shapes (64x96 by 96x32 and 64x32 by 32x96) emit and validate.
- `test_coopmat2_s_tiles` - The cm2 s-stamp tile shapes at the 32-deep and 64-deep k steps build through the name-parsed marker rail.
- `test_coopmat2_i8_tiles` - The int8 workgroup tiles with s32 and f32 64x64 accumulators build through the marker rail.

### test_enum.das

- `test_enum_value_rail` - An enum lowers to its underlying int in SPIR-V.
- `test_enum_struct_member` - An enum used as a struct member, a local and a result lowers to its underlying int.
- `test_enum_uint8` - An enum over uint8 lowers to OpTypeInt 8 0.

### test_fail_closed.das

- `test_fail_closed_rejections` - Every shader-illegal construct in the _fail_closed fixtures fails to compile with its specific diagnostic and no silent blob.
- `test_fail_closed_kernel_class` - A malformed [spirv_kernel] class or misused [spirv_decode] method fails to compile with the specific class-frontend diagnostic.
- `test_conf_rejects_spirv` - The over-wide conformance types and lattice layouts the SPIR-V emitter cannot spell fail to compile with a CPU-only or unsupported-type diagnostic.

### test_fragment.das

- `test_fragment_realism` - A fragment shader using discard, derivatives, textureSize and gl_FragDepth emits the matching opcodes and validates.
- `test_early_fragment_tests` - early_fragment_tests emits the EarlyFragmentTests execution mode and validates.
- `test_fragment_barycentric` - A @pervertex input read through gl_BaryCoordEXT emits PerVertexKHR, BaryCoordKHR and FragmentBarycentricKHR and validates.

### test_functions.das

- `test_userfn_value` - User functions with value parameters, transitive and shared helpers and vector in/out lower to OpFunctionCalls.
- `test_userfn_ref` - By-reference parameters lower through copy-in and copy-out temporaries.
- `test_userfn_inline` - spirv_inline helpers are visited in place instead of called.
- `test_userfn_inline_unrolled` - An inlined tail return inside a caller's unroll_full loop lowers correctly.
- `test_userfn_inline_method` - spirv_inline kernel-class methods inline a self-method chain.
- `test_userfn_inline_lazy` - A spirv_inline self-method whose ternary arm indexes a member array stays lazy.
- `test_userfn_global` - A helper that reads a module global lowers and validates.

### test_kernel_class.das

- `test_kernel_class_shape` - A class kernel emits the expected opcode shape and decorations.
- `test_kernel_class_twin_equivalence` - A class kernel emits the same per-opcode counts as its module-globals twin.
- `test_kernel_class_methods` - Method calls in a class kernel devirtualize to OpFunctionCalls with self dropped.
- `test_kernel_class_inheritance` - Base-class members are inherited and an override devirtualizes to the derived body.
- `test_kernel_class_validates` - Class kernel modules are accepted by spirv-val.
- `test_kernel_class_reflection` - Class kernel reflection reports the bindings and the push-constant range.

### test_loops.das

- `test_while_loop` - A while loop with break lowers to a structured OpLoopMerge.
- `test_range_for` - A range-for with continue lowers for both range(n) and range(lo, hi).
- `test_nested_loops` - Nested for-in-while loops with break and continue in both lower to a valid structured CFG.
- `test_elif_chain` - An if/elif/elif/else chain lowers to nested OpSelectionMerge.
- `test_early_return_in_loop` - An early return inside a for loop leaves a terminated then-block and a live merge.
- `test_unroll_full` - for unroll_full with literal bounds or a module constant emits copies with indices folded to constants.
- `test_runtime_for_and_bool_local` - A runtime urange bound and a bool local lower to a loop and a Function OpVariable.

### test_math.das

- `test_glsl_std450_breadth` - Every reachable math builtin maps to its GLSL.std.450 ext-inst sub-opcode.
- `test_glsl_std450_breadth_stage2` - The hyperbolic functions, fmod, mad, radians and degrees map to their GLSL.std.450 sub-opcodes.
- `test_glsl_std450_step` - step and smoothstep map to the GLSL.std.450 Step and SmoothStep.
- `test_fmod_vs_mod` - mod lowers to OpFMod and fmod to OpFRem, on scalars and on vectors.

### test_matrix.das

- `test_mvp_vertex` - A vertex shader multiplying a UBO mat4x4 MVP lowers to MatrixTimesMatrix, MatrixTimesVector and VectorTimesScalar with a local swizzle.
- `test_matrix_ctor` - float4x4 built from four columns emits one matrix OpCompositeConstruct and a OpMatrixTimesVector that validates.
- `test_matrix_var_local` - A var matrix local becomes a Function-storage variable and *= emits OpMatrixTimesMatrix.
- `test_matrix_ctor3` - float3x3 built from columns and read back by m[i] emits OpCompositeConstruct and OpCompositeExtract.
- `test_vector_times_matrix` - v * m emits OpVectorTimesMatrix and a const-column module matrix emits an OpConstantComposite.
- `test_vector_times_matrix3` - float3 * float3x3 emits the width-3 OpVectorTimesMatrix.

### test_mesh.das

- `test_mesh_stage_scaffolding` - An empty mesh shader declares its capability, extension, execution model and modes and calls SetMeshOutputsEXT.
- `test_task_stage_scaffolding` - An empty task shader declares its capability, extension, execution model and LocalSize and ends in EmitMeshTasksEXT.
- `test_mesh_output_config` - max_vertices, max_primitives and output_topology lower to the matching execution modes.
- `test_mesh_output_arrays` - Per-vertex and per-primitive output arrays lower to gl_MeshVerticesEXT and gl_PrimitiveTriangleIndicesEXT.
- `test_mesh_user_outputs` - User per-vertex varyings, @per_primitive outputs and per-primitive builtins lower to the mesh output variables.
- `test_mesh_task_payload` - A @task_payload emits TaskPayloadWorkgroupEXT, a four-operand EmitMeshTasksEXT and a mesh-side read.
- `test_mesh_ubo_interface` - A mesh shader reading a UBO lists the Uniform variable in the OpEntryPoint interface at SPIR-V 1.4.
- `test_mesh_task_shared` - @workgroup memory and barrier work in mesh and task shaders.

### test_precise.das

- `test_precise_marks_every_float_op` - precise puts NoContraction on every float op, including the callee's and the vector product.
- `test_precise_class_kernel` - The spirv_kernel class form carries the precise property.
- `test_plain_twin_unmarked` - The plain twin of a precise kernel has the same float ops and no NoContraction.

### test_raster.das

- `test_vertex_passthrough` - A vertex passthrough emits Location-decorated in and out variables, gl_Position and a CompositeConstruct.
- `test_fragment_passthrough` - A fragment passthrough emits OriginUpperLeft and a CompositeConstruct of float4(vec3, 1.0).
- `test_vertex_index_builtins` - gl_VertexIndex and gl_InstanceIndex drive a procedural vertex position.
- `test_vertex_point_size` - gl_PointSize lowers to a BuiltIn PointSize output.
- `test_vertex_draw_id` - gl_DrawID lowers to a BuiltIn DrawIndex input with the DrawParameters capability.
- `test_fragment_point_coord` - gl_PointCoord lowers to a BuiltIn PointCoord input.
- `test_fragment_math` - gl_FragCoord with dot, sqrt and clamp lowers to the GLSL.std.450 math opcodes.
- `test_vertex_flat` - An int vertex output is auto-Flat, a @flat float output is Flat and a plain float output is not.
- `test_vertex_attribute_is_never_flat` - An int vertex input attribute takes no Flat decoration.
- `test_fragment_output_is_never_flat` - An int fragment output attachment takes no Flat decoration.
- `test_fragment_flat` - An int fragment input is auto-Flat, a @flat float input is Flat and a plain float input is not.

### test_raytracing.das

- `test_raygen_stage` - A raygen shader declares its execution model, capability, extension, payload and TLAS and passes the payload operand to OpTraceRayKHR.
- `test_miss_stage` - A miss shader declares the miss model, an incoming payload and the world-ray builtin.
- `test_closest_hit_stage` - A closest-hit shader declares a hit attribute, hit builtins and a second payload for its shadow trace.
- `test_ray_query_compute` - An inline ray query in a compute shader declares the capability, extension and type and emits the seven OpRayQuery opcodes.

### test_reflect.das

- `test_reflect_compute_ssbo` - Reflection of the compute square kernel reports one storage buffer at set 0 binding 0 and local size 64,1,1.
- `test_reflect_uniform_fragment` - Reflection of a fragment UBO shader reports one uniform buffer at 0,0 in the fragment stage.
- `test_reflect_uniform_vertex` - Reflection of the MVP vertex shader reports one uniform buffer at 0,0 in the vertex stage.
- `test_reflect_push_constant` - Reflection of a push-constant shader reports one range at offset 0 of size 20 and no descriptors.
- `test_reflect_sampler` - Reflection of a texture shader reports one combined image sampler at 0,0.
- `test_reflect_comparison_sampler` - Reflection of a shadow-sampler shader reports one comparison sampler at 0,0 in the fragment stage.
- `test_reflect_malformed` - Malformed reflection streams decode to empty without over-reading, over-allocating or panicking.
- `test_reflect_roundtrip` - Encoding then decoding a hand-built reflection returns the same reflection.

### test_scalar_widths.das

- `test_int16` - short2 and ushort values lower with the Int16 capability, a single narrowing UConvert, native 16-bit arithmetic and unsigned compares, by value and by reference.
- `test_int64` - A 64-bit visibility-buffer pack with atomicMax, and its shift-and-mask unpack back to 32 bits, emit native 64-bit opcodes.
- `test_int64_block` - int64 and uint64 UBO members lower with the Int64 capability and an OpTypeInt 64 and pass spirv-val.
- `test_float16` - half storage declares Float16 with the pack/unpack pair, filter math widens with one OpFConvert each way, and closed arithmetic stays native 16-bit.
- `test_float64` - double storage declares Float64 with one OpFConvert each way, closed arithmetic stays native 64-bit with two-word literals, and an int widens straight to double.
- `test_storage_8_16` - An 8/16-bit std430 block lays out tight, pulls the storage capabilities and extension, and its small-int loads and stores narrow and widen correctly.

### test_ssbo.das

- `test_ssbo_array` - An array of @ssbo arrays becomes a descriptor array of storage buffers with one OpAccessChain per access.
- `test_ssbo_vector_elements` - @ssbo arrays of float2, float3 and float4 get std430 ArrayStrides of 8, 16 and 16.
- `test_ssbo_struct_elements` - An @ssbo array of structs lowers to a std430 element struct with chained field access.
- `test_ssbo_readonly` - @readonly marks the SSBO variable NonWritable, not the deduplicated block member.
- `test_ssbo_coherent` - @coherent decorates only its own SSBO variable and leaves a plain SSBO beside it undecorated.
- `test_ssbo_struct` - An @ssbo struct becomes a single-struct StorageBuffer Block whose member reads lower.

### test_storage_image.das

- `test_storage_image_compute` - An image2D lowers to a read-write Rgba8 OpTypeImage with imageLoad and imageStore.
- `test_image_size_query` - imageSize on a storage image emits OpImageQuerySize and the ImageQuery capability.
- `test_module_scope_const` - Module-scope let constants fold to OpConstant and OpConstantComposite.
- `test_storage_image_format` - An unannotated image2D stays Rgba8 while @format=r32f yields an R32f OpTypeImage.
- `test_storage_images` - image3D, image2DArray and imageCubeArray lower to the OpTypeImage operand tuples glslang emits.

### test_struct.das

- `test_struct_local` - A struct local becomes a zero-initialised Function variable with access-chained fields, works as an out-param and holds a fixed-array field without an ArrayStride.
- `test_struct_param` - A struct value parameter spills to a Function local with a run-time indexed array member, and a directly called spirv_decode method is a plain OpFunctionCall with the index bitcast to uint.
- `test_local_struct_member` - A member read of a local struct value copied from an SSBO element lowers to OpCompositeExtract.

### test_swizzle.das

- `test_global_swizzle` - A multi-component global swizzle loads then emits OpVectorShuffle and a single-component one emits OpAccessChain.
- `test_write_swizzle_per_lane` - A write-swizzle emits one AccessChain, CompositeExtract and Store per lane, never load-shuffle-store.
- `test_write_swizzle_lane_offset` - l.yzw = rhs writes destination lanes 1, 2 and 3 from source lanes 0, 1 and 2.

### test_texture.das

- `test_sampler_fragment` - A fragment shader sampling a sampler2D emits an OpTypeImage and OpTypeSampledImage in UniformConstant storage and an implicit-lod sample.
- `test_sampler_cube_array` - textureLod on a samplerCubeArray with a float4 direction-and-layer lowers to OpImageSampleExplicitLod.
- `test_explicit_lod_and_fetch` - textureLod and texelFetch lower to ExplicitLod sampling and OpImage plus OpImageFetch in a compute shader.
- `test_texture_grad` - Explicit-gradient sampling of 2D, 3D, cube and 2D-array images in compute emits the Grad image operand.
- `test_depth_compare` - textureCompare on a sampler2DShadow lowers to OpImageSampleDrefImplicitLod.
- `test_separate_image_sampler` - A texture2D and a separate sampler emit standalone image and sampler types combined by OpSampledImage.
- `test_texel_buffer` - texelFetch on a textureBuffer emits OpImageFetch on Dim Buffer with no OpImage and no Lod operand.
- `test_texel_fetch_array` - texelFetch on a sampler2DArray with an int3 coordinate and lod emits OpImage and OpImageFetch on an arrayed 2D image.
- `test_sampler_dims` - samplerCube, sampler3D and sampler2DArray emit OpTypeImage with the Cube, 3D and Arrayed dimensions.
- `test_subpass_input` - A subpassInput global read through subpassLoad lowers to OpImageRead.

### test_ubo.das

- `test_ubo_fragment` - A @uniform struct becomes a Uniform Block with std140 offsets and OpAccessChain member reads.
- `test_ubo_nested` - A uniform block with an array of vec4, a nested struct and an array of structs gets the right ArrayStrides, inner Offsets and access chains.
- `test_push_constant_fragment` - A @push_constant struct becomes a PushConstant Block with no descriptor and working member reads.

### test_vec.das

- `test_vec_compare` - Whole-vector == and != reduce through OpAll and OpAny to a scalar bool and validate.
- `test_vec_convert` - Same-width vector kind conversions lower to OpConvert and OpBitcast on vectors and validate.
- `test_vec_index` - v[i] extracts from a value base and chains through an addressable base, and textureLod on a sampler3D works.
- `test_vec_mod` - uvec3 % uvec3 is a single native OpUMod on a v3uint.
- `test_vec_scalar_arith` - Vector divided by a scalar splats the scalar operand for FDiv and SDiv, in plain and compound forms.
- `test_vec_shift` - vecN >> int splats the shift count to an int vector.
- `test_vector_arithmetic` - Component-wise vector +, -, unary - and a folded constant operand lower to the matching vector opcodes.
- `test_vector_times_scalar` - vec *= scalar emits OpVectorTimesScalar for constant and runtime scalars, not a shape-mismatched OpFMul.
- `test_int_vec_scalar` - An integer vector times an int splats the scalar with OpCompositeConstruct and multiplies with OpIMul.

### test_xmod.das

- `test_return_paths` - An if/else whose branches both return closes its merge block with OpUnreachable and the module passes spirv-val.
- `test_struct_value` - A plain struct passed as a parameter and returned as a result, plus a local whose initializer was dropped, emits an undecorated OpTypeStruct that spirv-val accepts.
- `test_xmod_array_store` - A fixed-array element store in a function from a required module is not dropped: its blob matches the same-file copy and both pass spirv-val.

### uncategorized.das

- `test_golden_disassembly` - The disassembly of every emitter fixture matches its frozen golden text.
- `test_color_mapping_spirv` - The color mapping helpers compile as a SPIR-V fragment shader.
- `test_stage_io_enabled` - @enabled = false excludes a stage output from the interface and the module validates.
- `test_spec_constants` - Spec constants emit OpSpecConstant shapes with distinct SpecIds and a WorkgroupSize composite that validates.
- `test_mrt_three_outputs` - A fragment shader with three @location outputs emits all three output variables.
- `test_binding_name_resolves` - Named @binding, @set and local_size_x constants resolve to the constants' values.
- `test_nonuniform_ext_marker` - nonuniformEXT(x) emits OpCopyObject, a NonUniform decoration and the capability and extension.
- `test_sampler_descriptor_array` - A sampler2D array sampled through nonuniformEXT(idx) emits an array type, an access chain and the non-uniform cascade.

- `test_const_float_bitkey` - The builder keys float constants by bits, so 0.0 and -0.0 stay distinct while deduplication still works.
- `test_private_global` - A @private_global becomes a Private-storage variable used as per-invocation scratch.
- `test_pack_half_spirv` - Half pack and unpack lower to GLSL.std.450 ext-insts and validate.
- `test_const_array_triangle` - A constant array indexed by gl_VertexIndex emits an array type, a constant composite and an access chain.
- `test_runtime_array_literal` - A fixed-array literal of runtime elements emits one OpCompositeConstruct and an OpStore, not a constant.
- `test_float_atomic_add` - A float atomicAdd on an SSBO vector component emits the float atomic add with its capability.
- `test_sdot4` - sdot4 emits the OpSDot shape with its capabilities and extension and validates.
- `test_subgroup_ops` - Subgroup ops lower to OpGroupNonUniform opcodes with the right group operation and capabilities, a dynamic broadcast Id raises the module to SPIR-V 1.5, and the ops are legal outside a workgroup stage.

- `test_opcode_census` - The set of opcodes the emitter produces across all fixtures equals the declared opcode set.

## stddlg/

### test_tray.das

Linux tray over a private session bus: this daslang spawns `dbus-daemon`, then a child daslang running the tray fixture with DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS pointing at it, and drives the child's StatusNotifierItem and dbusmenu objects with `dbus-send`. Registration with a real watcher is the daslinux VM's job (the panel shows the icon); everything else is asserted here.

- `test_tray_windows_smoke` - on Windows the tray fixture reaches ready on an interactive desktop, or reports unavailable
- `test_tray_macos_status_item` - on macOS a System Events click on the status item arrives in the tray as a click event
- `test_tray_over_private_bus` - the tray item exposes its StatusNotifierItem properties on a private D-Bus and Activate and ContextMenu arrive as click and right_click events
- `test_tray_menu_over_private_bus` - the tray menu layout carries labels, separator and checked or disabled entries over D-Bus, a clicked entry reports its id, and Quit ends the child
- `test_tray_icon_validation` - a tray icon whose byte count is not width times height times 4, or whose size is zero or negative, is rejected, and a matching one passes

### failed_tsi_gate_not_bool.das

### test_basic.das

- `test_grammar_forms` - a type macro is usable in the name(args), $name(args), name<types>(args) and $name<types>(args) forms
- `test_const_arguments` - a type macro takes bool and int constant arguments that change the shape and size of the result and composes with structs
- `test_typedecl_payload` - typedecl(expr) resolves to the type of the expression
- `test_shift_after_type_list` - shift and rotate operators still parse after a name<types> type macro form

### test_template_struct_instance.das

- `test_tsi_class_rail` - a class template instance stamps its methods, folds static_if, lets an override win and keeps constant defaults for a second instance
- `test_tsi_struct_rail` - two instances of one struct template fold their own constants into the field initializers
- `test_tsi_base_class` - a template own base class survives reification
- `test_tsi_cross_module` - a template required from another module can be instantiated
- `test_tsi_cross_module_base` - a template deriving from a concrete class of another module keeps that class as its parent
- `test_tsi_late_bind` - an alias supplied by another macro after reification is bound at infer time
- `test_tsi_call_rebind` - @template_call rebinds calls and function addresses per instance
- `test_tsi_gated_fields` - a gated field exists only where its axis enables it, in both polarities, and a dead static_if arm may reference a gated-off field
- `test_tsi_method_annotation_apply` - methods stamped by a template get their function-annotation applies
- `test_tsi_template_chain` - a chain of templates reifies whole, with constants, typedefs and overrides at every level and a template-level method override under a concrete parent
- `test_template_structure_class` - instances of a template structure class built for int and float run redo and undo and keep their own values and execution counts
